# SCA Papers Explorer: all papers

> All 2,064 Society of Core Analysts symposium papers, one line each: title (linked to the PDF), ID, year, authors, method, keywords and TL;DR. Grouped by topic (largest first), most central (PageRank) first within a topic.

TL;DRs, summaries, keywords and method labels were written by Claude (Sonnet 5.5) from each paper's text and can contain errors; titles, authors and years come from the papers themselves. Check the PDF before relying on a detail. Per-topic files with longer summaries: https://mralbu.github.io/sca-papers/llms.txt

## Digital rock and pore network modelling

- [Automated Mineral Identification of Sandstone Samples Using SEM/Image Analysis Techniques](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-09EURO.pdf) — SCA1991-09EURO, 1991. Theo W. Fens, Jos H.M. Bonnie, William D. Clelland. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: SEM/EDX, backscattered electron imaging, automated mineralogy, image analysis, pseudo elemental ratios, matrix acidising. An automated SEM/EDX/image-analysis method quantifies mineralogy, grain texture and pore structure in epoxy-impregnated sandstone, cutting unclassified objects from 8% to under 1% and guiding acid selection.
- [Improved Pore Network Extraction Methods](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-20.pdf) — SCA2005-20, 2005. A.P. Sheppard, R. M. Sok, H. Averdunk, Applied Mathematics. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: pore network extraction, medial axis transform, pore merging, micro-CT, percolation threshold, homotopic thinning. A parallel medial-axis pore network extraction method with topology-preserving, dynamically updated pore merging is applied to micro-CT images of two sandstones and a limestone, giving robust networks.
- [A Lattice-Boltzmann Based Method Applied to Digital Rock Characterization of Perforation Tunnel Damage](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-058.pdf) — SCA2016-058, 2016. Bernd Crouse, David M Freed, Nils Koliha, Gana Balasubramanian, Derek Bale, Stephen Zuklic. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: lattice-Boltzmann method, perforation damage, micro-CT digital rock, surfel boundary condition, absolute permeability, Berea sandstone. A surfel-boundary lattice-Boltzmann method accurately predicts permeability at coarse resolution and is used to map porosity and permeability damage around a perforation tunnel in Berea sandstone.
- [Quantitative 3D Characterisation of the Pore Space of Real Rocks: Improved µ-CT Resolution and Pore Extraction Methodology](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_17.pdf) — SCA2007_17, 2007. S. Youssef, E. Rosenberg, N. Gland, S. Bekri, O. Vizika. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: micro-CT, pore network extraction, skeletonization, mercury intrusion simulation, Fontainebleau sandstone, carbonate microporosity. A lab micro-CT and skeleton-based pore partitioning workflow extracts pore networks, simulating mercury intrusion and permeability that match experiments in sandstones but not heterogeneous carbonates.
- [Direct Hydrodynamic Simulation of Multiphase Flow in Porous Rock](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-014.pdf) — SCA2013-014, 2013. D. Koroteev, O. Dinariev, N. Evseev, D. Klemin, S. Safonov, S. Berg, C. van Kruijsdijk, R. Armstrong, M. T. Myers, L. Hathon, H. de Jong. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: direct hydrodynamic simulation, diffuse interface, capillary desaturation curve, pore-filling events, synchrotron micro-CT, digital rock. A GPU-based diffuse-interface pore-scale simulator (DHD) is validated against classical pore-scale displacement, micromodel, core-flood and synchrotron micro-CT data, showing good agreement for two-phase flow.
- [Large two phase Digital Rock Physics simulations for relative permeability uncertainty assessment](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2021/SCA2021-007.pdf) — SCA2021-007, 2021. Mohamed Regaieg, Igor Bondino, Clément Varloteaux, Titly Farhana Faisal, Jianhui Yang, Richard Rivenq. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pore network modelling, relative permeability, film flow oil-wet, network stitching, finite size effect, residual oil saturation. A parallelized pore-network workflow with stitched extraction and a revised film-flow model simulates plug-scale images, matches microplug and SCAL relative permeability, and shows finite-size effects on Sor.
- [A Comparative Study of Digital Rock Physics and Laboratory SCAL Evaluations of Carbonate Cores](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-24.pdf) — SCA2010-24, 2010. A. Grader, M.Z. Kalam, J. Toelke, Y. Mu, N. Derzhi, C. Baldwin, M. Armbruster, T. Al Dayyani, A. Clark, G. Bin-Dhaaer Al Yafei, B. Stenger. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: digital rock physics, lattice Boltzmann, carbonate reservoir rock types, Archie exponents, relative permeability, drainage capillary pressure. Digital rock physics results on Abu Dhabi carbonate plugs are compared with laboratory SCAL data, showing generally satisfactory agreement in about three months versus over two years.
- [Computations of Porosity and Permeability of Sparic Carbonate Using Multi-Scale CT Images](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2009/SCA2009-31.pdf) — SCA2009-31, 2009. Abraham S, Andrew B.S. Clark, Abu Dhabi, Taha Al-Dayyani, Amos Nur. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: multi-scale micro-CT, Lattice Boltzmann method, digital rock physics, carbonate permeability, relative permeability, core panoscopy. Multi-scale registered micro-CT (8, 4, 2 micron) and Lattice Boltzmann simulation give porosity, permeability and relative permeability of a heterogeneous carbonate, reasonably matching laboratory data.
- [Anchoring Methodologies for Pore-Scale Network Models: Application to Relative Permeability and Capillary Pressure Prediction](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-15.pdf) — SCA2001-15, 2001. Steven R McDougall, John Cruickshank, Ken S Sorbie. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pore network model, mercury injection capillary pressure, R-plot, gas-oil relative permeability, non-uniqueness, coordination number. Pore network models anchored to MICP data fit 8 samples' R-plots but poorly predict gas-oil relative permeability, because parameter combinations are non-unique.
- [Digital Core Laboratory: Rock and Flow Properties Derived from Computer Generated Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2006/SCA2006-21.pdf) — SCA2006-21, 2006. P.E. Øren, S. Bakke, H.G. Rueslåtten. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: digital rock physics, geologically based reconstruction, pore network modeling, Lattice Boltzmann permeability, Amott wettability index, waterflood relative permeability. Geologically reconstructed sandstone models match micro-CT permeability, formation factor and elastic moduli, and network modeling predicts waterflood relative permeabilities, with residual oil rising with initial water saturation.
- [Pore Shapes and Pore Geometry of Reservoir Rocks from µ-CT Imaging and Digital Image Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-093.pdf) — SCA2016-093, 2016. Matthias Halisch, Mayka Schmitt, Celso Peres Fernandes. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: µ-CT imaging, pore shape classification, Feret caliper, watershed segmentation, sandstone, 3D image analysis. Compares bounding-box, equivalent-diameter and Feret caliper descriptors for 3D pore shape classification in µ-CT images of three sandstones, finding Feret calipers deviate least from true pore geometry.
- [Pore network simulations coupled with innovative wettability anchoring experiment to predict relative permeability of a mixed-wet rock](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2022/SCA2022-10.pdf) — SCA2022-10, 2022. Mohamed Regaieg, Franck Nono, Titly Farhana Faisal, Clément Varloteaux, Richard Rivenq. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: digital rock physics, pore network modelling, wettability anchoring, ESRGAN super-resolution, mixed-wet small, relative permeability. A micro-CT wettability anchoring experiment constrains pore network simulations on an ESRGAN-enhanced Bentheimer image, and the predicted relative permeability agrees well with an in-house SCAL waterflood.
- [Multiscale Characterization of Reservoir Rock Microstructure: Combining Small-Angle Neutron Scattering and Image Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-35.pdf) — SCA2002-35, 2002. A.P. Radlinski, M.A. Ioannidis, A. L. Hinde, M. Hainbuchner, M. Baron, H. Rauch, S. R. Kline, Canberra City. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: small-angle neutron scattering, surface fractal, polydisperse spherical pore model, backscatter SEM autocorrelation, mercury intrusion porosimetry, NMR T2 relaxation. Combining SANS/USANS with BSE image analysis gives a pore size distribution from 1 nm to hundreds of microns for a sandstone, consistent with MIP and NMR.
- [Quantitative Mineral Analysis by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1993/SCA1993-08.pdf) — SCA1993-08, 1993. Abigail Matteson, Michael M. Herron. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: FTIR spectroscopy, quantitative mineralogy, nonnegative least squares, clay mineral quantification, KBr pellet, opal-A quartz. A transmission FTIR pressed-pellet procedure with nonnegative least-squares spectral fitting quantifies 14 minerals in 49 synthetic mixtures to within ±1.2 wt %, without clay size separation.
- [Resolving Challenges in Analyzing Iron-Rich Samples by X-Ray Diffraction](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2023/SCA2023-047.pdf) — SCA2023-047, 2023. Salah Al-Ofi, Shouxiang Ma. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: X-ray diffraction, Rietveld refinement, siderite, Cu K-alpha fluorescence, mineral library, sample grinding contamination. Systematic XRD study of iron-rich Chelsea sandstone shows grinding contamination, Cu fluorescence background, and library/fitting-model choice strongly affect mineral identification and quantification.
- [Evaluation of the Reliability of Prediction of Petrophysical Data Through Imagery and Pore Network Modelling](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-33.pdf) — SCA2008-33, 2008. C. Caubit, G. Hamon, A.P. Sheppard. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: pore network modelling, X-ray micro-tomography, blind test, gas/oil relative permeability, drainage capillary pressure, residual gas saturation. A blind test of ANU X-ray micro-CT and Numerical Rocks thin-section pore network modelling against Total lab data finds reliable porosity and Pc only when microporosity and clay are captured.
- [A Framework to Validate Digital Rock Technology](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-28.pdf) — SCA2011-28, 2011. J. Schembre-McCabe, R. Salazar-Tio, G. Ball, J. Kamath, San Ramon. Method: review or workflow. Keywords: digital rock validation, experimental design, micro-CT segmentation, representative elementary volume, uncertainty analysis, pore network modeling. A framework compares digital rock computed property ranges, from experimental design on segmentation uncertainty, with laboratory uncertainty ranges; a sandstone example shows overlap for most properties except elastic ones.
- [Investigation into the Reliability of Predictive Pore-Scale Modeling for Siliciclastic Reservoir Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-23.pdf) — SCA2010-23, 2010. Olivier Lopez, Alexander Mock, Jostein Skretting, Egil Boye Petersen Jr, Pål-Eric Øren, Alf Birger Rustad. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pore-scale modeling, pore network model, Lattice-Boltzmann permeability, relative permeability, process-based rock reconstruction, Amott wettability index. Process-based pore-scale modeling of 28 Norwegian siliciclastic reservoir samples predicts porosity, permeability and oil-water relative permeability in good agreement with core data and field trends.
- [Pore-Scale Modelling: Effects of Network Properties on Predictive Capabilities](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-35.pdf) — SCA2012-35, 2012. Nasiru Idowu, Cyril Nardi, Haili Long, Pål-Eric Øren, Numerical Rocks. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pore network extraction, skeletonization, micro-CT, relative permeability, thinning algorithm, grain-based algorithm. Three skeletonization methods applied to micro-CT images of sandstones give different pore networks but similar multiphase flow predictions, which agree with grid simulations and experiments when topology is preserved.
- [Computation of Relative Permeability Functions in 3D Digital Rocks by a Fractional Flow Approach Using the Lattice Boltzmann Method](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-36.pdf) — SCA2012-36, 2012. Giuseppe De Prisco, Jonas Toelke, Moustafa R Dernaika, Abu Dhabi. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: lattice Boltzmann method, digital rock physics, relative permeability, fractional flow boundary conditions, representative elementary volume, mixed wettability. A GPU-based lattice Boltzmann method with PID-controlled inlet boundary conditions simulates fractional-flow drainage and imbibition relative permeability in a digital carbonate, matching experimental imbibition curves.
- [Statistical Synthesis of Image Analysis and Mercury Porosimetry for Multiscale Pore Structure Characterization](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-10.pdf) — SCA2003-10, 2003. E. Amirtharaj, M.A. Ioannidis, I.F. Macdonald. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: mercury intrusion porosimetry, surface fractal dimension, two-point correlation function, pore size distribution, pore-to-throat aspect ratio, BSEM image analysis. Combines BSEM image-derived two-point correlation with MIP fractal scaling to build pore size distributions over 0.01-1000 μm, revealing pore-to-throat aspect ratios in sandstones and carbonates.
- [Drainage and Imbibition Capillary Pressure Curves of Carbonate Reservoir Rocks by Digital Rock Physics](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-56.pdf) — SCA2012-56, 2012. Y. Mu, Q. Fang, C. Baldwin, J. Töelke, A. Grader, M. Dernaika, Z. Kalam, Abu Dhabi. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: digital rock physics, lattice Boltzmann, capillary pressure, drainage and imbibition, GPU, carbonate. Lattice Boltzmann simulations on a micro-CT image of a micritic carbonate predict drainage and imbibition Pc curves that reasonably match MICP and centrifuge data.
- [Pore Structure and Hydrodynamics in Sandstones](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1996/SCA1996-07.pdf) — SCA1996-07, 1996. G. Chauveteau, L. Nabzar, Y. El Attar, C. Jacquin. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: grain and pore throat model, permeability-porosity relation, Fontainebleau sandstone, polymer depletion, mercury injection, quartz overgrowth. A grain and pore throat model links permeability to grain size, porosity and hydrodynamic throat diameter; mercury injection overestimates throat size by 1.7–1.9 times in sharp-edged media.
- [Quantitative X-Ray CT for SCAL Plug Homogeneity Assessment](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-004.pdf) — SCA2013-004, 2013. Jos G. Maas, Albert Hebing. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: X-ray CT, Hounsfield units, mini-permeameter, permeability variation, plug homogeneity, beam hardening. A theoretical model links CT Hounsfield standard deviation to permeability variation in core plugs, validated against mini-permeameter data on 95 plugs, giving objective homogeneity screening limits.
- [Distribution of Clays in Sandstones by Image Analysis: Quantification, Representativity and Effects on Petrophysical Properties](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-14.pdf) — SCA1994-14, 1994. Claudine Durand. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: SEM image analysis, clay distribution, variogram representativity, covariance function, Kozeny-Carman permeability, sandstone. SEM backscattered image analysis quantifies clay distribution in sandstones, with variograms checking representativity; permeability formulas fit model sandstones but fail for North Sea reservoir sandstones.
- [Case Study in Validating Capillary Pressure Curves, Relative Permeability and Resistivity Index of Carbonates from X-Ray Micro Tomography Images](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-02.pdf) — SCA2010-02, 2010. Zubair Kalam, Taha Al Dayyani, Andrew Clark, Sven Roth, Cyril Nardi, Olivier Lopez, Pål-Eric Øren. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: X-ray micro tomography, pore network modeling, carbonate relative permeability, formation resistivity factor, saturation exponent, capillary pressure. Micro-CT images and pore-network modeling of three Middle East carbonate plugs predict permeability, resistivity and two-phase properties; they match lab data well except where unresolved microporosity matters.
- [Combining Electrical Measurements and Mercury Porosimetry to Predict Permeability](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-28.pdf) — SCA2012-28, 2012. Douglas Ruth, Dean Emeritus, Craig Lindsay, Core Specialist, Mark Allen, Lead Reservoir Engineer West Africa. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: mercury injection porosimetry, Purcell permeability model, formation factor, Archie equation, tortuosity, pore throat size distribution. Extends Purcell's equation using an REV model, combining mercury porosimetry and formation factor to predict permeability within a factor of two for 24 Ghana samples over seven decades.
- [3D Imaging and Flow Characterization of the Pore Space of Carbonate Core Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2006/SCA2006-23.pdf) — SCA2006-23, 2006. Mark Knackstedt, Christoph Arns, Abid Ghous, Arthur Sakellariou, Tim Senden, Adrian Sheppard, Rob Sok, Holger Averdunk, W. Val Pinczewski, Girija S. Padhy, Marios A. Ioannidis. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: micro-CT, digital rock physics, carbonate microporosity, pore network extraction, lattice Boltzmann permeability, MICP simulation. Micro-CT images of model, outcrop and reservoir carbonates give MICP, permeability and pore networks matching experiments, and a hybrid scheme accounts for microporosity in flow.
- [A Comparative Study of Three Pore-Scale Reconstruction and Pore-Network Extraction Techniques](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-36.pdf) — SCA2008-36, 2008. Arjen Cense, Fons Marcelis. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: pore-network modeling, micro-CT reconstruction, process-based reconstruction, pore architecture models, Lattice-Boltzmann permeability, primary drainage capillary pressure. Three third-party pore-scale reconstruction and network extraction methods (micro-CT, PAMs, process-based) are compared on a clay-rich sandstone; single-phase properties are predicted reasonably, primary drainage multiphase properties only partly.
- [Characterisation of Carbonate Reservoir Heterogeneity Using Probe Permeability Images, Petrography and Borehole Image Log Data](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-41.pdf) — SCA2001-41, 2001. Graham F. Aplin, Ajay K. Sapru. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: probe permeametry, borehole image logs, nodular limestone, image thresholding, permeability heterogeneity, karstification. Probe permeability maps, petrography and microresistivity image logs are combined to characterise permeability heterogeneity in a nodular limestone reservoir, using image thresholding to extend permeability classes beyond cored intervals.
- [Two-Phase Flow Rock-Typing : Another Approach](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-13.pdf) — SCA2003-13, 2003. Gerald Hamon, Miguel Bennes. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: relative permeability, rock-typing, wettability index, waterflood residual oil saturation, height above contact, coreflood sampling. Using Fontainebleau sandstone and two field cases, the paper shows pore-geometry rock-types fail for waterflood Kr when wettability varies; multivariate, process-dependent rock-types are needed.
- [Pore Network Models to Calculate Transport and Electrical Properties of Single or Dual-Porosity Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-35.pdf) — SCA2005-35, 2005. S. Békri, O. Vizika. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pore network model, resistivity index, saturation exponent, non-Archie behavior, mercury porosimetry, gas/oil relative permeability. A 3-D pore network model built from mercury porosimetry predicts Fontainebleau gas/oil relative permeability and resistivity index, showing pore-body/throat correlation and wettability control saturation exponent and non-Archie behavior.
- [Validation of Fundamental Carbonate Reservoir Core Properties Using Digital Rock Physics](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-19.pdf) — SCA2012-19, 2012. Olivier Lopez, Alex Mock, Pål Eric Øren, Haili Long, Zubair Kalam, Volker Vahrenkamp, Muhamed Gibrata, Samy Seraj, Soman Chacko, Mohamed Al Hammadi, Habeeba Al Hosni, Hani Sahn, Antonio Vizamora. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: digital rock physics, micro-CT upscaling, carbonate rock types, formation resistivity factor, primary drainage capillary pressure, NMR T2 relaxation. Multi-scale micro-CT imaging and upscaled digital rock modeling of 100+ Middle-Eastern carbonate plugs reproduces measured porosity, permeability, FRF, m, Pc and NMR T2 well.
- [Can Network Modelling Predict Two-Phase Flow Functions?](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-29.pdf) — SCA2011-29, 2011. K.S. Sorbie, A. Skauge. Method: review or workflow. Keywords: pore network modelling, a priori prediction, mixed wettability, relative permeability, digital rock, network extraction. Argues that a priori network-model prediction of kr, Pc and Sor in mixed-wet rocks needs ~15-26 parameters, more than the ~5-8 the data contain, so it is not true prediction.
- [Density Functional Hydrodynamics in Multiscale Pore Systems: Chemical Potential Drive](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-002.pdf) — SCA2019-002, 2019. Oleg Dinariev, Nikolay Evseev, Denis Klemin. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: density functional hydrodynamics, chemical potential drive, digital rock upscaling, subresolution porosity, steady-state relative permeability, carbonate. Upscales density functional hydrodynamics to a chemical potential drive model for unresolved pores, coupled with DFH in resolved pores, and validates it on a carbonate micro-CT model.
- [Prediction of relative permeability and fast wettability assessment using Digital Rock Physics: An operational study on a Reservoir Sandstone](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2023/SCA2023-026.pdf) — SCA2023-026, 2023. Mohamed Regaieg, Titly Farhana Faisal, Franck Nono, Fabrice Pairoys, Victor Fernandes, Cyril Caubit. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: digital rock physics, ESRGAN super-resolution, pore network modelling, wettability anchoring experiment, relative permeability, micro-CT. A blind-test DRP workflow (ESRGAN, pore network modelling, wettability anchoring) predicted waterflood relative permeability of a reservoir sandstone, agreeing with SCAL on the tested facies and a second facies.
- [Pore-Level Validation of Representative Pore Networks Obtained from Micro-CT Images](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_15.pdf) — SCA2007_15, 2007. J. Y. Arns, A. P. Sheppard, C. H. Arns, M. A. Knackstedt, A. Yelkhovsky, W. V. Pinczewski. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: pore network extraction, micro-CT, lattice Boltzmann permeability, throat volume factor, wetting phase connectivity, covering radius transform. Pore networks extracted from micro-CT images reproduce lattice-Boltzmann permeability for large volumes (>10,000 pores), while image-based analysis shows corner wetting phase disconnects as saturation falls.
- [Relative permeability assessment in a giant carbonate reservoir using Digital Rock Physics](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-03.pdf) — SCA2012-03, 2012. Zubair Kalam, Samy Seraj, Zahid Bhatti, Alex Mock, Pål Eric Øren, Vegar Ravlo, Olivier Lopez. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: digital rock physics, relative permeability, carbonate reservoir, pore network modeling, steady-state upscaling, micro-CT. Blind study comparing digital rock physics water-oil imbibition relative permeability with steady-state lab tests on carbonate rock types, finding good agreement when oil-wet wettability is assumed.
- [Improving Digital Rock Physics Predictive Potential for Relative Permeabilities from Equivalent Pore Networks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-017.pdf) — SCA2013-017, 2013. Nasiru Idowu, Cyril Nardi, Haili Long, Pål-Eric Øren, Igor Bondino. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pore network extraction, relative permeability, throat volume allocation, digital rock physics, Clashach sandstone, mercury injection capillary pressure. Pore network element lengths explain permeability differences between extracted networks, while pore volume allocated to throats explains counter-intuitive relative permeability trends; grid-computed Pc curves can constrain this allocation.
- [Rapid Mineral Analysis by Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1988/SCA1988-09.pdf) — SCA1988-09, 1988. Hamish Adam, Don Harville, Daniel Meer, David Freeman. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: FTIR spectroscopy, quantitative mineralogy, Beer's law, KBr pellet, clay minerals, log calibration. Describes the Mineralog FTIR method for rapid quantitative rock mineralogy, tested on synthetic mixtures to about 5 wt% accuracy, and its uses in log calibration and formation damage screening.
- [Dual-Range FT-IR Mineralogy and the Analysis of Sedimentary Formations](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1997/SCA1997-29.pdf) — SCA1997-29, 1997. Michael M. Herron, Abigail Matteson, Gale Gustavson. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: FT-IR mineralogy, far-IR spectroscopy, KBr pellet, mineral standards, kaolinite speciation, geochemical log lithology. Combining mid- and far-IR spectra with an expanded standards set improves quantitative FT-IR mineralogy of oilfield samples, validated by reconstructing measured elemental chemistry to about ±1 wt%.
- [The Uses of Surface Area Data Obtained on Reservoir Core Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-39.pdf) — SCA1998-39, 1998. Robert D East. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: specific surface area, irreducible water saturation, cation exchange capacity, Qv excess conductivity, cementation exponent, Kozeny-Carman. Surface area measured on Australasian reservoir cores correlates with permeability, irreducible water, CEC/Qv and cementation exponent, supporting its routine measurement for petrophysical interpretation.
- [Impact of Clay Mineral Attributes in Estimating Damage in Carbonate Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-38.pdf) — SCA2001-38, 2001. W.H. Al-Bazzaz, Kisr Engler. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: clay migration, electron probe microanalysis, X-ray diffraction, mercury porosimetry, formation damage, carbonate reservoirs. Combining XRD, electron microprobe mapping and mercury porosimetry on four low-permeability carbonate plugs shows clay size, location and distribution, not just amount, control clay migration damage.
- [An Integrated Approach to Compute Physical Properties of Core Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-057.pdf) — SCA2014-057, 2014. S. Linden, T. Cvjetkovic, E. Glatt, A. Wiegmann. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: digital rock physics, SIMPLE-FFT Stokes solver, LIR-tree, Explicit Jump method, pore morphology drainage, Berea sandstone compression. Five FFT-based and adaptive solvers compute permeability, conductivity, tortuosity, drainage, resistivity index and elasticity on one segmented Berea micro-CT image, including under compression, showing strong sensitivity to small compressions.
- [Reservoir Properties of Conventional Rock: Routine Measurements on Mini-Plugs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-081.pdf) — SCA2014-081, 2014. Dmitry Korobkov, Alexander Goncharov, Russian Federation. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: mini-plug, micro-CT, gas permeability, porosity measurement, steady-state relative permeability, upscaling. Conventional porosimeter and permeameter equipment was adapted for 8 mm mini-plugs; porosity, permeability and Bentheimer relative permeability matched 30 mm plugs within uncertainty for homogeneous rocks.
- [Determination of Physical Properties of Tight Porous Media Using Digital Core Physics/Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2015/SCA2015-052.pdf) — SCA2015-052, 2015. Shahin Ghomeshi, Saeed Taheri, Evgeny Skripkin, Sergey Kryuchkov, Apostolos Kantzas. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: SEM image reconstruction, tight rock, digital core physics, pore-scale simulation, upscaled permeability, NMR simulation. Reconstructs 3-D tight rock from three SEM images and simulates porosity, permeability, resistivity and NMR, giving an upscaled permeability of about 6.9 µD.
- [Modelling of Imbibition Relative Permeability by Direct Quasi-Static Approach](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-007.pdf) — SCA2016-007, 2016. S. Berg, M. Rücker, H. Ott, A. Georgiadis, H. van der Linde, F. Enzmann, M. Kersten, R. T. Armstrong, S. de With, J. Becker, A. Wiegmann. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: imbibition relative permeability, quasi-static morphological approach, synchrotron micro-CT, Euler characteristic, ganglion dynamics, connected pathway flow. Quasi-static morphological modelling of imbibition on Gildehauser sandstone is compared with synchrotron micro-CT and steady-state data; it fails to reproduce fluid connectivity and relative permeability.
- [A Closer Look at Shale: Representative Elementary Volume Analysis with Laboratory 3D X-Ray Computed Microtomography and Nanotomography](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-58.pdf) — SCA2011-58, 2011. Jeff Gelb, Allen Gu, Tiffany Fong, Luke Hunter, S H Lau, Wenbing Yun Xradia. Method: digital rock or imaging. Keywords: representative elementary volume, shale, X-ray nanotomography, watershed segmentation, digital core analysis, porosity. Multi-scale lab micro- and nano-CT imaging of shale is used to determine a representative elementary volume for porosity, found to be about 17,000 µm³.

## CO2 storage, hydrates and rock-fluid reactions

- [An Integrated Approach to Assess the Petrophysical Properties of Rocks Altered by Rock/Fluid Interactions (CO2 Injection)](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-03.pdf) — SCA2005-03, 2005. S. Bekri, O. Vizika. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: CO2 storage, rock/fluid interaction, carbonate dissolution, pore network model, mercury porosimetry, permeability-porosity evolution. Homogeneous acid alteration of two carbonates shows permeability gains of 30-70% for ~2 porosity units; pore network modeling identifies the dissolution scenario matching the data.
- [Displacement and Mass Transfer of CO2/Brine in Sandstone](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-05.pdf) — SCA2011-05, 2011. H. Ott, S. Berg, S. Oedai. Method: laboratory experiment. Unsteady-state CT-monitored CO2/brine floods in Berea sandstone give drainage kr and Pc by history matching, show stable displacement with channeling, and quantify CO2 dissolution effects.
- [Experimental Investigation of Cooling Effects Resulting from Injecting High Pressure Liquid or Supercritical CO2 into a Low Pressure Gas Reservoir](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-40.pdf) — SCA2008-40, 2008. Daniel R. Maloney, Marcos Briceno. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: Joule-Thomson cooling, CO2 injection, depleted gas reservoir, hydrate formation, CO2 phase change, slim tube. Flooding a 50 ft sand-packed tube with 3,500 psig CO2 showed Joule-Thomson cooling is masked by heat transfer at 198 °F, but liquid-to-vapor transition at room temperature caused ice/hydrate blockage.
- [SCA2010-20](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-20.pdf) — SCA2010-20, 2010. Method: laboratory experiment. Core floods show dry CO2 injection into brine-saturated sandstone causes local salt precipitation that cuts absolute permeability but not CO2 effective permeability, while SC H2S in dry limestone produces water.

## Coreflood interpretation and simulation

- [Computer simulation of Special Core Analysis (SCAL) flow experiments shared on the Internet](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1997/SCA1997-19.pdf) — SCA1997-19, 1997. J.G. Maas, A.M. Schulte. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: SCAL simulation, capillary end-effect, history matching, relative permeability, centrifuge, unsteady-state. Describes SCORES, a web-accessible Shell simulator for unsteady-state, steady-state and centrifuge SCAL experiments, and how history matching resolves relative permeability and capillary pressure interference.
- [A New Versatile Relative Permeability Correlation](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-32.pdf) — SCA2005-32, 2005. Frode Lomeland, Einar Ebeltoft, Wibeke Hammervold Thomas. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: LET correlation, relative permeability, steady-state experiment, history matching, Corey correlation, s-shaped oil relative permeability. Proposes the 3-parameter LET relative permeability correlation, showing it history-matches steady-state coreflood data where Corey and Chierici fail, and changes full-field water production forecasts.
- [Open Source Simulator Dumux Available for](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-08.pdf) — SCA2011-08, 2011. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: DuMux, SCAL simulation, porous plate, continuous injection, resistivity index, capillary end effect. The open-source DuMux simulator is adapted to simulate SCAL experiments (USS, SS, centrifuge, porous plate, continuous injection), validated against analytical solutions and MoReS, and used to analyze porous plate and CI measurements.
- [Simultaneous Determination of Relative Permeability and Capillary Pressure Using Data from Several Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-17.pdf) — SCA2004-17, 2004. A. Sylte, E. Ebeltoft, E.B. Petersen. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: history matching, relative permeability, capillary pressure, multi-speed centrifuge, steady state, covariance analysis. - [Strength Variations with Deformation in Unconsolidated Rock After Water Breakthrough](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-22.pdf) — SCA2002-22, 2002. Gang Han, Maurice B. Dusseault. Analytical liquid-bridge models for detached and squeezed spherical grains predict how capillary strength of unconsolidated sand varies with water saturation and strain, weakening faster under compression.
- [Experimental Results for High Flow Rates of Oil-Water Through High Permeability Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-17.pdf) — SCA2003-17, 2003. S. Abdobal, M. Fourar, R. Lenormand. - [Water Oil Relative Permeability Comparative Study: Steady Versus Unsteady State](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-77.pdf) — SCA2005-77, 2005. Celso C.M. Branco, Euclides J. Bonet. ## Core-log petrophysical integration

- [Archie'S Dream: Petrophysics from Sidewall Samples and Cuttings](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-05.pdf) — SCA1998-05, 1998. T.W. Fens, M.A. Kraaijveld, R. Visser. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: SEM backscattered electron imaging, sidewall samples, cuttings, image analysis porosity, Carman-Kozeny permeability prediction, multiple linear regression. Porosity and permeability are predicted from SEM/BSE images of small samples via regression on about 250 plugs, with R 0.94 and 0.89 and validation on 32 samples.
- [A Fast and Direct Method of Permeability Measurement on Drill Cuttings](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-23.pdf) — SCA2002-23, 2002. P. Egermann, R. Lenormand, D. Longeron, C. Zarcone. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: drill cuttings permeability, trapped gas compression, pressure diffusion, viscous oil injection, history matching, rig-site measurement. A fast method measures permeability of drill cuttings by viscous-oil invasion compressing trapped gas, history-matched with a diffusion model, agreeing with core permeability from 0.1 to 2000 md.
- [Reservoir Rock Properties of Devonian Shale from Core and Log Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1989/SCA1989-10.pdf) — SCA1989-10, 1989. D.L. Luffel, F. Kent Guidry. Sheng Ding, Tai Pham, El Paso. Method: field or reservoir case study. Keywords: J-function, saturation-height function, free water level, tight gas, capillary pressure, log calibration. An Excel-based J-function saturation-height tool (JMOD) calibrates log analysis to core capillary pressure, giving free water level and Sw in tight gas reservoirs, shown in three case studies.
- [Characterization of the Pore Space Accessed by the Non-Wetting Phase During Constant Rate Injection at the Breakthrough Capillary Pressure](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-35.pdf) — SCA2004-35, 2004. A modified subison pore system classification analyzes constant-rate injection pressure traces in network simulations and a mercury micromodel; the micromodel behaves like correlated networks.
- [Dynamics of Capillary Flow and Transport Properties in Carbonate Sedimentary Formation by Time-Controlled Porosimetry](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-44.pdf) — SCA2004-44, 2004. A. Time-controlled mercury porosimetry on four carbonate textures is analysed with an extended Washburn equation to get capillary flow dynamics and pore filling times, showing capillary-fingering flow.
- [Relationship Between Capillary Pressure and Resistivity Index](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-14.pdf) — SCA2005-14, 2005. Kewen Li. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: capillary pressure, resistivity index, fractal model, porous plate, Archie saturation exponent, low permeability. A fractal-based power-law model linking capillary pressure to resistivity index is tested on 14 cores and fits well, especially at low permeability, outperforming Szabo's linear model.
- [Investigation of Critical Capillary Number for Gas-Water System Through Experiment and Reservoir Simulation](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-27.pdf) — SCA2005-27, 2005. Minghua Ding, Apostolos Kantzas. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: critical capillary number, residual gas saturation, spontaneous imbibition, forced imbibition, gas compressibility, NMR saturation monitoring. Spontaneous and forced water imbibition with NMR monitoring plus simulation show the critical capillary number for remobilizing trapped gas (2e-8) is far below that for oil-water (2e-5).
- [A Valid Approach to Correct Capillary Pressure Curves- a Case Study of Berea and Tight Gas Sands](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2009/SCA2009-41.pdf) — SCA2009-41, 2009. Gbenga M. Funmilayo, Shameem Siddiqui. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: high-pressure mercury injection, capillary pressure correction, blank correction, rock compressibility, tight gas sands, Berea sandstone. A modified blank correction for mercury injection capillary pressure, using non-porous quartz runs to account for system compressibility, matters for Berea but not for tight gas sands.
- [Extracting Pore Throat Size and Relative Permeability from MRI Based Capillary Pressure Curves](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2009/SCA2009-46.pdf) — SCA2009-46, 2009. Derrick P. Green. MRI-based centrifuge capillary pressure curves with many data points yield pore throat size distributions, NMR relaxivity and Burdine-model relative permeability without needing a fitted Pc model.
- [Drainage Capillary Pressure and Resistivity Index from Short-Wait Porous Plate Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-46.pdf) — SCA2010-46, 2010. Moustafa Dernaika, Ove B. Keywords: porous plate, resistivity index, primary drainage capillary pressure, short-wait method, exponential decay model, carbonate. Short-wait porous plate drainage tests on carbonates give the same RI-Sw relationship as equilibrium tests in one third of the time, with Pc derived by exponential fitting.
- [Entry Pressure Measurements Using Three Unconventional Experimental Methods](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-02.pdf) — SCA2011-02, 2011. P.F. Boulin, P. Bretonnier, V. Vassil, A. Four gas entry pressure methods (standard, dynamic, racking, residual) were compared on a carbonate and a claystone caprock; dynamic is fastest, residual underestimates PE.
- [Hysteresis of Capillary Pressure, Resistivity Index and Relative Permeability in Carbonate Rock Types](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-14.pdf) — SCA2011-14, 2011. Drainage-imbibition hysteresis in Pc, resistivity index and steady-state Kr was measured on Middle East carbonate rock types, showing strong, rock-type-dependent hysteresis and non-Archie imbibition RI.
- [An Integrated Approach to Estimate Threshold Capillary Pressure from Core and Log Data](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-020.pdf) — SCA2013-020, 2013. K. Djaouti, P. Egermann, P. - [Thin Section Image Analysis for Estimation of Initial Water Saturation in Siliciclastic Reservoir Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-070.pdf) — SCA2013-070, 2013. - [Transition Zone Behaviour: The Measurement of Bounding and Scanning Kr and Pc Curves at Reservoir Conditions for a Giant Carbonate Reservoir](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-004.pdf) — SCA2014-004, 2014. - [Oil Recovery in the Transition Zone of Carbonate Reservoirs with Wettability Change: Hysteresis Models of Relative Permeability Versus Experimental Data](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-007.pdf) — SCA2014-007, 2014. - [On the Role of Sub-Core Scale Heterogeneity During Repeated Drainage/Imbibition Cycles in a Sandstone](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-024.pdf) — SCA2016-024, 2016. Ronny Pini. - [Stress Sensitivity of Mercury Injection Measurements](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-011.pdf) — SCA2017-011, 2017. P. Guise, C. Grattoni, Q.J. Fisher, A. Schiffer. - [An integrated workflow for MICP integration, pore typing and saturation height modeling – Poster # 62](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-062.pdf) — SCA2017-062, 2017. Philippe Rabiller. ## Centrifuge capillary pressure methods

- [Simple and Accurate Methods for Converting Centrifuge Data into Drainage and Imbibition Capillary Pressure Curves](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-07.pdf) — SCA1991-07, 1991. P. Forbes. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, Hassler-Brunner inversion, forced imbibition, USBM wettability index, ill-conditioned inversion. Two analytical methods invert the centrifuge equation for drainage and imbibition capillary pressure; the second needs no smoothing or fitting and matches artificial and experimental data well.
- [Water-Oil Capillary Pressure and Wettability Measurements Using Micropore Membrane Technique](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-26.pdf) — SCA1994-26, 1994. Daniel LONGERON, Wibeke L. HAMMERVOLD. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: micropore membrane, capillary pressure hysteresis, wettability index, Amott index, USBM index, porous plate. A micropore membrane coreholder measures full four-curve water-oil capillary pressure cycles in days, and a new area-based HL wettability index is proposed and tested on sandstone and carbonate.
- [A Novel Method for the Determination of Water/Oil Capillary Pressures of Mixed Wettability Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1993/SCA1993-22.pdf) — SCA1993-22, 1993. R. Lenormand, A. Eisenzimmer. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: capillary pressure, mixed wettability, semi-dynamic method, ultrasonic saturation measurement, negative capillary pressure, USBM wettability index. A semi-dynamic steady-flow method with outlet washing and ultrasonic saturation measurement gives full positive and negative capillary pressure cycles for sands and Berea of varying wettability without membranes.
- [Centrifuge Data Analysis Techniques : An Sca Survey on the Calculation of Drainage Capillary Pressure Curves from Centrifuge Measurements](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1997/SCA1997-14.pdf) — SCA1997-14, 1997. Pierre Forbes. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, inversion of centrifuge data, radial correction, Hassler-Brunner solution, interlaboratory survey, synthetic data. An SCA survey tests about 19 centrifuge capillary pressure interpretation solutions on ten synthetic datasets, finding geometry-dependent errors up to 10 saturation units and only a few reliable methods.
- [Advances in Centrifuge Methodology for Core Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1990/SCA1990-11.pdf) — SCA1990-11, 1990. M. J. King, K. R. Narayanan, A. J. Falzone. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: centrifuge gravity drainage, Hassler-Brunner analysis, stretched exponential extrapolation, history matching, oil relative permeability, capillary pressure. Reviews centrifuge capillary pressure analyses, presents an automated ultracentrifuge and stretched-exponential extrapolation, and shows history matching with fixed Pc gives less biased oil relative permeability than simultaneous Pc estimation.
- [Calculation of Capillary Pressure Curves from Data Obtained by the Centrifuge Method](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1988/SCA1988-02.pdf) — SCA1988-02, 1988. Douglas Ruth. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, Hassler-Brunner equation, van Domselaar method, Bentsen parameter estimation, linear interpolation method. Compares centrifuge capillary pressure data reduction methods, introduces a linear interpolation method that matches Bentsen's parameter estimation on simulated data, and recommends using multiple methods.
- [Comparative Study of Drainage Capillary Pressure Measurements Using Different Techniques and for Different Fluid Systems](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-24.pdf) — SCA1994-24, 1994. Lionel Sabatier. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: drainage capillary pressure, centrifuge, porous plate, mercury injection, interfacial tension scaling, clay content. Drainage capillary pressure on six water-wet samples compared across porous plate, centrifuge and mercury injection and three fluid pairs; gas-liquid data do not transfer to oil-brine.
- [Capillary Pressure From Centrifuge —A New, Direct Method](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-24EURO.pdf) — SCA1991-24EURO, 1991. Hroar Hermansen. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, Volterra integral equation, Hassler-Brunner method, forced imbibition, modified midpoint method, mercury injection. A direct modified-midpoint solution of the centrifuge Volterra equation gives capillary pressure curves without iteration, validated on synthetic data, nine cores against diaphragm and mercury methods, and forced imbibition.
- [Comparison Study of Capillary Pressure Curves Obtained Using Traditional Centrifuge and Magnetic Resonance Imaging Techniques](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_30.pdf) — SCA2007_30, 2007. Derrick P. Green, Josh R. Dick, John Gardner, Bruce J. Balcom, Bing Zhou. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: capillary pressure, centrifuge, SPRITE MRI, saturation profile, Leverett J function, Hassler-Brunner. Centrifuged core plugs are scanned with 1D centric-scan SPRITE MRI to get saturation profiles and capillary pressure curves, matching traditional centrifuge results with 3-5 times fewer speeds.
- [Interpretation of centrifuge data using local saturation](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-28.pdf) — SCA1994-28, 1994. M. Fleury, R. Lenormand, F. Deflandre. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, ultrasonic local saturation, multi-speed centrifuge, relative permeability, forced imbibition, wettability. Ultrasonic local saturation measured during multi-speed centrifuge runs matches computed Pc curves on water-wet to oil-wet samples but does not improve relative permeability determination.
- [Oil/Water Imbibition and Drainage Capillary Pressure Determined by MRI on a Wide Sampling of Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-01.pdf) — SCA2008-01, 2008. Derrick P. Green, Josh R. Dick, Mike McAloon, P.F. de J. Cano-Barrita, Jon Burger, Bruce Balcom. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: SPRITE MRI, centrifuge capillary pressure, imbibition and secondary drainage, D2O brine, T2 cutoff, Brooks-Corey fit. A centrifuge combined with quantitative SPRITE MRI saturation profiles gives drainage and imbibition capillary pressure curves from few centrifuge speeds, including negative Pc portions, tested on sandstone and chalk.
- [Experimental Measurements of Capillary Pressure and Relative Permeability Hysteresis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-23.pdf) — SCA2001-23, 2001. Shehadeh K. Masalmeh. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: capillary pressure hysteresis, contact angle hysteresis, wettability change, water trapping, scanning curves, Pc-probe. Measures capillary pressure and relative permeability hysteresis on water-wet and non-water-wet cores, proposing a model based on trapping, contact angle hysteresis and wettability change.
- [Analysis of Centrifuge Relative Permeability Data](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1997/SCA1997-11.pdf) — SCA1997-11, 1997. Douglas Ruth. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: centrifuge relative permeability, history matching, Corey exponents, Bentsen capillary pressure, sensitivity analysis, speed ramp-up. Simulation of multi-speed centrifuge drainage shows wetting-phase exponents are well determined, non-wetting exponents poorly so, and capillary pressure should be fitted separately; ignoring speed ramp-up biases results.
- [Local Saturation Measurement While Centrifuging (MWC) for Improving Centrifuge Capillary-Pressure Curve Determination](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-15.pdf) — SCA1992-15, 1992. P. Forbes, C. Chardaire-Rivière, F. Deflandre, M. Fleury. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, ultrasonic transit time, local saturation measurement, Hassler-Brunner boundary condition, Vosges sandstone, CT scanner calibration. Ultrasonic transit-time measurements at three core locations during centrifuging give local saturations and direct capillary pressure curves, and show centrifuge assumptions can fail at fairly low speeds.
- [A Method for Measuring in-Situ Capillary Pressures at Different Wettabilities Using Live Crude Oil at Reservoir Conditions, Part 1: Feasibility Study](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-18.pdf) — SCA2002-18, 2002. Arne Graue, Thomas Bognø, Eugene A. Spinler, Bernard A. Baldwin. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: nuclear tracer imaging, centrifuge capillary pressure, in-situ saturation, Na-22 tracer, collimator geometry, Portland chalk. A nuclear tracer imaging system on a centrifuge measures in-situ saturations during spinning; feasibility tests on chalk show reproducible saturations and a plausible primary drainage Pc curve.
- [Radial effect and sample heterogeneity effect on centrifuge capillary pressure curves](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1995/SCA1995-34.pdf) — SCA1995-34, 1995. M. FLEURY, P. FORBES. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, radial effect correction, sample heterogeneity, porous plate, drainage, double porosity. Centrifuge experiments at different radii confirm and validate a radial-effect correction, and show that centimeter-scale heterogeneity makes capillary pressure curves depend on sample orientation.
- [Capillary Pressure Scanning Curves by Direct Measurement of Saturation by](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1997/SCA1997-05.pdf) — SCA1997-05, 1997. E. A. Spinler, B. A. Baldwin. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: capillary pressure scanning curves, MRI saturation profile, centrifuge, frozen octadecane, imbibition hysteresis, free water level. Centrifuge-established saturation profiles, frozen in place with octadecane and mapped by MRI, give direct capillary pressure drainage and imbibition scanning curves for Berea sandstone and chalk.
- [Calillary Pressure Curve Measurement Using a Single-Moderate-Speed Centrifuge and Quantitative Magnetic Resonance Imaging](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-44.pdf) — SCA2005-44, 2005. Quan Chen, Bruce J. Balcom. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, SPRITE MRI, saturation profile, Berea sandstone, mercury intrusion porosimetry, single-speed centrifuge. A single-speed centrifuge run on a long core, with 1D SPRITE MRI saturation profiling, gives a drainage capillary pressure curve matching mercury intrusion for Berea sandstone.
- [Centrifuge Capillary Pressure Data Interpretation: Gravity Degradation Aspect Consideration](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-25.pdf) — SCA1994-25, 1994. Zhigang Andy CHEN, Douglas W. RUTH. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, gravity degradation, three-dimensional centrifuge theory, equipotential surfaces, parameter estimation, Beckman centrifuge. A 3D centrifuge theory including gravity at low rampup speeds is used to interpret capillary pressure, showing 2D models misestimate the high-saturation zone for high-permeability sandstones.
- [Simultaneous Measurement of Multiple Capillary Pressure Curves from Wettability and Rock Property Variations Within Single Rock Plugs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-57.pdf) — SCA1999-57, 1999. E. A. Spinler, B. A. Baldwin, A. Graue, Bartlesville OK. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: centrifuge capillary pressure, local saturation, Forbes method, Hassler-Brunner, spline interpolation, quality control. Proposes quality control of centrifuge local saturation by numerically recalculating average saturation, showing the continuous Forbes method outperforms the standard discrete Forbes calculation with few points.

## Stress, compressibility and acoustic velocity

- [Measurement of Pore Compressibility Characteristics in Rock Exhibiting "Pore Collapse" and Volumetric Creep](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-24.pdf) — SCA1991-24, 1991. J. M. Hamilton, J. L. Shafer. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: pore collapse, volumetric creep, pore compressibility, reservoir compaction, loading rate correction, diatomite. Hydrostatic compaction and creep tests on diatomite and carbonate show fast lab loading overestimates pore-collapse stress; a log-rate extrapolation corrects compaction predictions to field depletion rates.
- [Laboratory Measurement of Oil/Water Saturations by an Ultrasonic Technique](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-11EURO.pdf) — SCA1992-11EURO, 1992. F. Deflandre, R. Lenormand. Ultrasonic sound-velocity calibration for oil/water saturation in cores during imbibition is linear for So 0.2-0.5, can use effluent mass balance, but is highly temperature sensitive.
- [Mechanical Properties Analysis: The Key to Understanding Petrophysical Properties Stress Sensitivity](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1993/SCA1993-21.pdf) — SCA1993-21, 1993. R.A. Farquhar, B.D.G. Synthetic sandstone made under stress and then unloaded and reloaded shows that coring stress release permanently lowers velocities by 9-12% and inflates measured stress dependence.
- [Stress Sensitivity of Saturation and End-Point Relative Permeabilities](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-11.pdf) — SCA2001-11, 2001. C. Jones, A. A. Al-Quraishi, J. M. Somerville, S. A. - [Interpretation and Reliability of Laboratory Tests Measuring Porosity, Pore Compressibility, and Velocity on Unconsolidated Deep Offshore Reservoirs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-21.pdf) — SCA2002-21, 2002. - [Insights into Low Salinity Water Flooding](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2018/SCA2018-039.pdf) — SCA2018-039, 2018. Hasan N. Al-Saedi, Ralph E. Flori, Patrick V. Brady. Method: laboratory experiment. ## Gas permeability and tight rock measurement

- [Quantification of Permeability Variations Across Thin Laminae in Cross Bedded Sandstone](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-02EURO.pdf) — SCA1992-02EURO, 1992. Alle Brendsdal, Christian Halvorsen. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: probe permeameter, laminae, permeability anisotropy, crossbedded sandstone, arithmetic and harmonic averaging, well test permeability. Probe permeameter measurements on plugs, cubes and whole core quantify lamina-scale permeability in crossbedded Statfjord sandstone and give a unit permeability estimate consistent with well test.
- [Measurement of "Rock Properties" in Coal for Coalbed Methane Production](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-19.pdf) — SCA1991-19, 1991. Bruce W. Gash. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: coalbed methane, cleat porosity, miscible displacement tracer, gas-water relative permeability, fines migration, JBN unsteady-state method. Modified core-analysis methods on undried coal cores give cleat porosity near 2% or less, declining water permeability, and consistent gas-water relative permeability from unsteady- and steady-state tests.
- [Permeability Measurement on Small Rock Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-32.pdf) — SCA2010-32, 2010. R. Lenormand, F. Bauget, Gabriel Ringot Cydarex. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: Klinkenberg effect, pulse decay permeability, resin disc, nanoDarcy permeability, Darcylog, inertial effects. Resin-disc, miniplug, Darcylog and open-surface pulse-decay methods measure permeability on cm-scale samples from sub-nanoD to Darcy, interpreted with Klinkenberg and inertial numerical models.
- [Klinkenberg Permeability Measurements: Problems and Practical Solutions](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-20EURO.pdf) — SCA1991-20EURO, 1991. Colin A. McPhee, Kevin G. Arthur. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: Klinkenberg permeability, gas slip factor, backpressure flow mode, non-Darcy flow, Forchheimer equation, net effective stress. Shows Klinkenberg permeability and slip factor depend strongly on flow mode, transducer accuracy, sleeve pressure and non-Darcy flow, and recommends backpressure measurement and corrections.
- [Permeability Characterization on Tight Gas Samples Using Pore Pressure Oscillation Method](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-30.pdf) — SCA2010-30, 2010. Y. Wang, R. J. Knabe. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: pore pressure oscillation, tight gas permeability, Klinkenberg permeability, FFT amplitude attenuation, phase shift, storage capacity. Applies a sinusoidal pore pressure oscillation permeameter with FFT analysis to tight gas and shale samples, finding good agreement with steady-state Klinkenberg permeability and better accuracy at microdarcy levels.
- [Steady State Stress Dependent Permeability Measurements of Tight Oil Bearing Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-012.pdf) — SCA2014-012, 2014. Shreerang S. Chhatre, Edward M. Braun, Somnath Sinha, Matthew D. Determan, Quinn R. Passey, Timothy E. Zirkle, Alex C. Wood, Jeff A. Boros, Daniel W. Berry, Sergio A. Leonardi, Ryan A. Kudva. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: steady-state liquid permeability, stress creep, net confining stress, permeability hysteresis, capillary standards, Vaca Muerta tight oil. A steady-state liquid permeability method for intact tight oil plugs under net confining stress, validated with capillary standards, shows strong stress creep, permeability decline and hysteresis.
- [The Effects of Cleat Orientation and Confining Pressure on Cleat Porosity, Permeability and Relative Permeability in Coal](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-24.pdf) — SCA1992-24, 1992. Bruce W. Gash, Richard F. Volz, Gary Potter, John M. Corgan. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: coal cleat, gas-water relative permeability, confining pressure, permeability anisotropy, unsteady-state method, coalbed methane. Measurements on La Plata coal show cleat orientation does not affect gas-water relative permeability, while raising confining pressure from 450 to 1000 psig cuts permeability about fivefold.
- [A Detailed Analysis of Permeability and Klinkenberg Coefficient Estimation from Unsteady-State Pulse-Decay or Draw-Down Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_08.pdf) — SCA2007_08, 2007. Yves Jannot, Didier Lasseux, Guillaume Vizé, Gérald Hamon. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: pulse-decay permeability, Klinkenberg coefficient, draw-down experiment, sensitivity analysis, tight rock gas permeability, inverse estimation. A 1D gas-flow model with Klinkenberg effect and sensitivity analysis identify optimal pulse-decay/draw-down conditions for estimating permeability and Klinkenberg coefficient from a single pressure decay; draw-down is best.
- [Non-Darcy Flow in Core Plugs: A Practical Approach](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-19EURO.pdf) — SCA1991-19EURO, 1991. Stuart J. Morrison, Terry P. Duggan. Derives a permeability-dependent limiting gas flow rate keeping non-Darcy pressure loss under 1% in routine plug measurements, using Forchheimer β–k correlations from 46 Morecambe Bay plugs.
- [Low Permeability Measurements Using Steady-State and Transient Methods](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_07.pdf) — SCA2007_07, 2007. P. Carles, P. Egermann, R. Lenormand, JM. Lombard. Compares steady-state, pulse-decay, Darcygas and Darcylog gas permeability methods and mercury-injection correlations on tight caprock samples after Klinkenberg correction; unsteady-state reads about twice steady-state.
- [Permeability, Porosity and Klinkenberg Coefficient Determination on Crushed Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-32.pdf) — SCA2011-32, 2011. - [Principles, Practice and Applications of Laboratory Minipermeametry](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1990/SCA1990-26EURO.pdf) — SCA1990-26EURO, 1990. Christian Halvorsen, Andrew Hurst. Describes Statoil's automated laboratory minipermeameter, its calibration against Hassler-sleeve plugs and an analytical solution, core handling changes, and applications showing dense grid data reveal heterogeneity missed by plugs and logs.
- ["Correlations of Liquid and Air Permeabilities for Use in Reservoir Engineering Studies"](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1990/SCA1990-12.pdf) — SCA1990-12, 1990. Virgil J. Pugh, David C. Thomas. Correlates air permeability with oil and brine permeability for 1868 samples, showing air permeability approximates liquid permeability and can predict effective oil permeability in a clayey reservoir, cutting costs.

- [Gas Migration Through Self-Sealed or Intact Claystone](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2015/SCA2015-046.pdf) — SCA2015-046, 2015. Yang Song, C. A. Davy, F. Skoczylas, CS Villeneuve. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: gas breakthrough pressure, Callovo-Oxfordian claystone, snap-off, self-sealing, gas permeability, mass spectrometer. Gas breakthrough in water-saturated COx claystone occurs first by discontinuous capillary snap-off then continuous flow; self-sealed samples break through at 1.45-3 MPa versus about 4.4-5.4 MPa undisturbed.
- [Determining gas permeability in tight rocks: How do we know if we are obtaining the right value?](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-010.pdf) — SCA2016-010, 2016. Carlos A. Grattoni, Samuel Allshorn, Quentin J. Fisher. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: gas permeability standards, Klinkenberg slip factor, pulse-decay permeability, capillary reference plugs, Hagen–Poiseuille, tight rocks. Capillary-based reference plugs (11 nD to 5.9 mD) with calculable permeability validate steady-state and pulse-decay gas permeameters and show the Klinkenberg constant C depends on capillary size.
- [Alternative Approaches for Transient-Flow Laboratory-Scale Permeametry](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-061.pdf) — SCA2016-061, 2016. Michael J. Hannon Jr. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: pressure-pulse decay, shale permeability, crushed rock permeametry, radial flow, particle size distribution, pseudo-pressure. Proposes analytical models for bidirectional and radial pulse-decay permeametry and for crushed particles with a size distribution, cutting test times by roughly 8-18 times versus conventional pulse decay.
- [Klinkenberg Permeability by Pressure Decay on Tight Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-066.pdf) — SCA2016-066, 2016. Xiangmin Zhang, Albert Hebing. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: Klinkenberg permeability, pressure decay, pressure pulse decay, Brace method, gas slippage factor, tight rocks. Compares steady-state, pulse decay and pressure decay Klinkenberg permeability on four tight samples; pressure decay processed with Brace's method matches steady-state, while Jones' method overestimates.
- [New Approach to Evaluation of Coal Permeability in Underground Coal Mines (CBM)](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-097.pdf) — SCA2016-097, 2016. Budak P, Szpunar T, Leśniak G. Method: field or reservoir case study. Keywords: coal permeability, coalbed methane, confining pressure, slug test, fracture permeability, packer injection test. Compares laboratory coal permeability at confining pressures with in situ slug and injection well tests in a Silesian mine, finding rough agreement around 0.1–0.4 mD.
- [Workflow for Measurement of Steady-State to Liquid Permeability in Nano-Darcy Reservoir Rock](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-038.pdf) — SCA2017-038, 2017. Robert L. Krumm, James J. Howard, Houston TX. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: steady-state permeability, nano-Darcy shale, micro-CT screening, NMR T2 relaxation, decane saturation, crushed rock analysis. A workflow combining micro-CT crack screening, NMR liquid volumes and steady-state decane flow measures nano-Darcy matrix permeability in shale plugs, giving values one to two orders below crushed-rock results.
- [Application of Core Analysis Techniques for Tight Rocks for the Investigation of Borehole Cement](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-049.pdf) — SCA2017-049, 2017. Marisa B. Rydzy, James Heathman, Chad Broussard, Jorge Patino, Nours Elmetni, Aaron Dhaemers, Matthias Appel. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: borehole cement, water permeability, nano-Darcy permeability, MICP pore-throat size, NMR T2, MXCT bubble analysis. Shale-type permeability, NMR, MICP and MXCT methods applied to five borehole cements show nano-Darcy water permeability controlled by pore-throat size, with bubbles negligible and dried gas permeability inflated.
- [A Comparative Study of Shale Pore Structure Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-092.pdf) — SCA2017-092, 2017. R. Cicha-Szot, P. Budak, G. Leśniak, P. Such. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: Klinkenberg gas slippage, pulse decay permeability, mercury intrusion capillary pressure, nitrogen adsorption, FIB-SEM, shale pore size. Pore sizes of ten Baltic Basin shales from Klinkenberg slippage under stress are compared with MICP, nitrogen adsorption and SEM; unstressed methods overestimate effective flow pore size in clay-rich samples.
- [Reconsidering Klinkenberg'S Permeability Data](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2018/SCA2018-001.pdf) — SCA2018-001, 2018. Douglas Ruth, Rasoul Arabjamaloei. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: Klinkenberg coefficient, gas slippage, Darcy permeability, mean free path, tortuosity, effective pore diameter. Reanalysis of Klinkenberg and Ash and Grove gas permeability data shows a second-order correction gives marginal gains, while Ash-Grove data yield pore diameter and tortuosity estimates.
- [Insights, Trends and Challenges Associated with Measuring Coal Relative Permabiltiy](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2018/SCA2018-005.pdf) — SCA2018-005, 2018. Dylan Shaw, Peyman Mostaghimi, Furqan Hussein, Ryan T. Armstrong. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: coal relative permeability, effective stress, history matching, modified Brooks-Corey, cleat compression, unsteady-state drainage. Unsteady-state helium-brine floods on one Gloucester Basin coal at three effective stresses, history matched with modified Brooks-Corey, show rising gas end-point kr, Swi and cross-point with stress.
- [Gas Slippage in Partially Saturated Tight Rocks and During Drainage](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-033.pdf) — SCA2019-033, 2019. Gas permeability and slippage were measured on tight sandstones at partial water saturation and during NMR-monitored drainage; capillary redistribution dominates at high saturation, slippage at low.
- [Validation of Simulated Relative Permeability Estimates in Very Low Permeability Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-046.pdf) — SCA2019-046, 2019. A minimal measurement workflow validates image-based relative permeability simulations in an organic-rich shale, showing cracks strongly affect flow and permeability measured under different stress.
- [New method for characterising the nano- to macro-scale voidage within black shale and for modelling shale gas recovery efficiency](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-058.pdf) — SCA2019-058, 2019. Combines helium pycnometry and mercury intrusion on intact 1 cm3 black shale samples with PoreXpert inverse and forward modelling to map voids from 1 nm to 6 µm.

- [A priori simulation of relative permeabilities of intact subsamples of tight oil shale from a hydraulic fracturing play](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2023/SCA2023-014.pdf) — SCA2023-014, 2023. - [The effect of sample anisotropy properties, dimensions, and imposed noflow boundaries on the measurement of directional permeability and viscous resistivity](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2023/SCA2023-034.pdf) — SCA2023-034, 2023. Jacob McGregor. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: anisotropic permeability tensor, viscous resistivity, diameter-to-length ratio, no-flow boundary, apparent directional permeability, Darcy's law. Numerical simulations show that in anisotropic cores, permeability needs thin discs (D/L≫1) with sealed sides, while viscous resistivity suits long rods (D/L≪1); approximate analytical solutions estimate errors.
- [A novel approach to gas cycling enhanced oil recovery (GCEOR) evaluation in unconventional porous media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2024/SCA2024_1011.pdf) — SCA2024_1011, 2024. F. A patented radial-flow core apparatus enables full-condition gas-cycling EOR tests on nanodarcy Montney and Duvernay rock; geology controls response and gas utilization is low.
- [Developing Correlation for Porosity and Permeability Between Mercury Intrusion and Gas Expansion Methods for Sandstone Core Plugs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2024/SCA2024_1089.pdf) — SCA2024_1089, 2024. - [Image Registration: Enhancing and Calibrating X-Ray Micro-CT Imaging](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-35.pdf) — SCA2008-35, 2008. Shane Latham, Trond Varslot, Adrian Sheppard. ## Gas condensate and trapped gas

- [Capillary End Effects and Gas Production from Low Permeability Formations](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-26.pdf) — SCA2005-26, 2005. Richard Christiansen, Carolina Mayoral, Carlos Pereira. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: water block, capillary end effect, low permeability gas, hydraulic fracturing leakoff, Brooks-Corey relative permeability, liquid loading. Simulations with 1D in-house and commercial reservoir models show water blocks from fracturing leakoff and imbibition cut gas production in low permeability formations by up to about 30%.
- [Laboratory Measurement of the Residual Gas Saturation](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1991/1-SCA1991-23EURO.pdf) — SCA1991-23EURO, 1991. Jean DELCLAUD. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: residual gas saturation, gas trapping, trapped gas diffusion, spontaneous imbibition, waterflooding, Land correlation. Compares waterflood and capillary-rise methods for residual gas saturation in poorly consolidated sandstones, showing trapped-gas diffusion matters at ambient but not reservoir conditions, and proposes simplified procedures.
- [Distribution of Trapped Gas Saturation in Heterogeneous Sandstone Reservoirs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-14.pdf) — SCA2001-14, 2001. SUZANNE Karine, HAMON Gérald, BILLIOTTE Joël, TROCME Vincent. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: maximum residual gas saturation, spontaneous imbibition, Fontainebleau sandstone, clay content, gas trapping, porosity trends. About 360 spontaneous imbibition measurements on reservoir and Fontainebleau sandstones show maximum trapped gas saturation is controlled by porosity and clay content, with clay lowering Sgrm.
- [Depressurization Under Tertiary Conditions in the Near-Wellbore Region: Experiments, Visualization and Radial Flow Simulations](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-15.pdf) — SCA2003-15, 2003. P. Egermann, S. Banini, O. Vizika. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: depressurization, critical gas saturation, gas relative permeability, tertiary conditions, micromodel visualization, radial flow simulation. Core, micromodel and radial simulations show tertiary depressurization gives lower gas relative permeability than secondary, and Sgc varies with distance from the wellbore.
- [Gas Phase Relative Permeability Characterization on Tight Gas Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-13.pdf) — SCA2011-13, 2011. Y. Wang, Z. Chen, V. Morah, R. J. Knabe, M. Appel. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: gas relative permeability, pressure falloff, tight gas, Corey exponent, evaporation method, Klinkenberg slip factor. A toluene evaporation plus nitrogen pressure-falloff method measures gas relative permeability on tight cores quickly; about 30 cores fit Corey exponents of ~2 (drainage) and ~3 (imbibition).
- [Residual Gas Saturation of Sample Originally at Residual Water Saturation in Heterogeneous Sandstone Reservoirs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-14.pdf) — SCA2003-14, 2003. SUZANNE Karine, HAMON Gérald, BILLIOTTE Joël, TROCME Vincent. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: residual gas saturation, Land's law, spontaneous imbibition, controlled evaporation, irreducible water saturation, NMR clay bound water. Sixty sandstone samples show residual gas saturation at irreducible water equals maximum trapped gas saturation, controlled by rock quality rather than Swir, so Land's law extrapolation is invalid.
- [Mobilisation of Trapped Gas from Below the Gas-Water Contact](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-29.pdf) — SCA2004-29, 2004. A. Cable, D. Mogford, M. Wannell. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: trapped gas saturation, depressurisation, critical gas saturation, in-situ saturation monitoring, gas-brine relative permeability, filamentous illite. Depressurisation of a 3 mD reservoir core composite with trapped gas at 117 barg showed gas mobilised after only 6-7% expansion, with extremely low relative permeabilities.
- [Measurement of Relevant Gas Condensate Relative Permeability Data for Well Deliverability Predictions for a Deep Marine Sandstone Reservoir](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-33.pdf) — SCA2003-33, 2003. Steady-state gas condensate corefloods on four deep marine sandstones give krg as a function of krg/kro and capillary number, and the data significantly reduce simulated well productivity.
- [Effect of Capillary, Viscous and Gravity Forces on Gas Condensate Mobility](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-24.pdf) — SCA2002-24, 2002. F. Kalaydjian. Method: theory or analytical model. A fractal capillary-bundle model predicts gas-condensate relative permeability and critical condensate saturation from capillary and Bond numbers, matching literature data without adjustable parameters.
- [A New Method to Determine Critical Gas Saturation and Relative Permeability During Depressurization in the Near-Wellbore Region](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2000/SCA2000-36.pdf) — SCA2000-36, 2000. - [Experimental Techniques for the Measurement of Relative Permeability and in-Situ Saturation in Gas Condensate Near Well Bore and Drainage Studies](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-28.pdf) — SCA1999-28, 1999. Andrew Cable, Robert Mott, Mike Spearing. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. - [Impact of Deformation Bands on Fluid Flow and Oil Recovery](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-45.pdf) — SCA2010-45, 2010. G. Ersland, A. Graue, R.W. Moe. Method: laboratory experiment. ## CO2, carbonated water and WAG injection

- [Mechanisms of Oil Recovery by Carbonated Water Injection](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2009/SCA2009-26.pdf) — SCA2009-26, 2009. Mehran Sohrabi, Masoud Riazi, Mahmoud Jamiolahmady, Shaun Ireland, Chris Brown. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: carbonated water injection, micromodel, oil swelling, CO2 dissolution, tertiary recovery, pore-scale visualisation. High-pressure micromodel tests show tertiary carbonated water injection recovers extra oil from n-decane (32.7%) and viscous oil (11.8%) mainly through oil swelling and coalescence.
- [Mechanisms of Extra-Heavy Oil Recovery by Gravity-Stable CO2 Injection](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-20.pdf) — SCA2008-20, 2008. Mehran Sohrabi, Alireza Emadi, Mahmoud Jamiolahmady, Shaun Ireland, Chris Brown. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: heavy oil, CO2 injection, micromodel visualisation, oil viscosity reduction, double displacement, asphaltene. High-pressure micromodel experiments show gravity-stable CO2 injection dilutes extra-heavy oil, enabling large additional recovery in subsequent waterflooding, while water presence hinders CO2 performance.
- [Pore Scale Investigation of Carbonated Water Injection with and without Gravity](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-037.pdf) — SCA2016-037, 2016. S. Mahdavi, L.A James, T.E Johansen. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: carbonated water injection, micromodel, residual oil saturation, gravity effect, capillary and Bond number, oil film flow. Glass micromodel experiments compare water flooding and carbonated water injection in horizontal and vertical orientations and at two rates; CWI lowers residual oil to about 50% versus 64% for water flooding.
- [Carbonated Water Flood: What We Observed in Sand Pack Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-34.pdf) — SCA2011-34, 2011. Yannong Dong, Claudia Ishizawa, Ed Lewis, Birol Dindoruk. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: carbonated water flooding, sand pack, CO2 solubility, oil viscosity reduction, injection rate, enhanced oil recovery. Eight sand pack floods with viscous oil compare carbonated water and water flooding at four injection rates; carbonated water improves recovery and 2 PV/day is judged optimal.
- [Improved Oil Recovery and Injectivity by Carbonated Water Injection](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-05.pdf) — SCA2012-05, 2012. M. Sohrabi, M. Tavakolian, A. Emadi, M. Jami, S. Ireland. Coreflood tests on Clashach sandstone show carbonated water injection, secondary or tertiary, increases oil recovery, delays water breakthrough and lowers differential pressure versus plain waterflood.
- [Using MRI to Study in Situ Oil Recovery During CO2 Injection in Carbonates](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-41.pdf) — SCA2008-41, 2008. A. Brautaset, G. Ersland, A. Graue, J. Stevens, J. Howard. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: CO2 injection, MRI saturation imaging, chalk, supercritical CO2, oil swelling, wettability. MRI monitored waterflood and miscible liquid or supercritical CO2 injection in four Portland chalk cores at different wettabilities; CO2 after waterflood gave the highest recovery, up to 93.6% OOIP.
- [Pore-scale experimental investigation of in-situ wettability and displacement mechanisms governing WAG in oil-wet carbonates](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-038.pdf) — SCA2019-038, 2019.
