Micro-CT imaging of a miniature Fond du Lac carbonate core during aging and three WAG cycles shows how gas shielding improves sweep and recovery, diminishing after two cycles.
- [Gas Displacement Efficiency for a Low Permeability Carbonate Field](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-05.pdf) — SCA2004-05, 2004. A. Cable, M. Spearing, J. Bahamaish, Y. Dabbour, Z. Kalam. Reservoir-condition miscible gas, water, tertiary gas and WAG floods on a 52 cm carbonate composite show recovery rising linearly with initial gas slug size, with water blocking.

Corefloods on McElroy field rock types showed no rock-type explanation for WAG water injectivity loss; a crude/CO2 soaked core showed injectivity loss from asphaltene plugging.
- [Effects of Paraffin Wax Precipitation During Cold Water Injection in a Fractured Carbonate Reservoir](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-28.pdf) — SCA2004-28, 2004. D. Maloney, A. Oesthus. Coreflods, ESEM imaging and thermal simulation show wax precipitation from cold seawater injection in chalk barely harms injectivity or recovery, so heating injection water is not justified.
- [An Experimental Approach of CO2 Sequestration in Gas Condensate Reservoirs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2006/SCA2006-35.pdf) — SCA2006-35, 2006. E. Shtepani, F.B. Thomas. - [Investigation of Water Flooding and Carbonated Water Injection (CWI) in a Fractured Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-058.pdf) — SCA2017-058, 2017. Sedigheh Mahdavi, L.A. Glass micromodel experiments show carbonated water injection beats water flooding in fractured porous media, with and without gravity, through better sweep, later breakthrough and higher recovery.

- [Improving oil recovery by injecting alcohol-treated CO₂](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-091.pdf) — SCA2019-091, 2019. Saira Saira, Emmanuel Ajoma, Furqan Hussain. ## In-situ saturation monitoring in coreflooding

- [In-Situ Saturation Distributions: The Key to Understanding Core Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-05.pdf) — SCA1994-05, 1994. P Naylor, D A Puckett. Method: review or workflow. Reviews gamma attenuation, X-ray attenuation and gamma emission methods for in-situ saturation measurement in core floods, with accuracy analysis and wettability and gravity drainage examples.

A PEEK Hassler microcell combined with lab micro-CT images oil/water distribution through a full drainage-imbibition cycle in Fontainebleau sandstone, revealing trapping configurations, IFT effects and hysteresis in interfacial area.
- [State-of-the-art X-ray Steady State Apparatus for advanced core flow studies. SCA-9853](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-53.pdf) — SCA1998-53, 1998. J.G.C. Coenen, P. Koornneef.. Schwing. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: X-ray saturation monitoring, low salinity waterflooding, Welge weighing under back pressure, Dean-Stark, unsteady-state coreflood, calibration scans. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: coreholder head geometry, volume of fluid CFD, waterflooding, variogram sill, flow front homogeneity, residual oil saturation. CFD (VOF) simulations of brine-oil waterflooding in a core show that coreholder head geometry changes front homogeneity and oil production by up to 32%, favoring a triangular groove design.
- [Geometric Optimization of Coreholder Head Designs in Coreflooding Experiments Using CFD](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2026/SCA2026-055.pdf) — SCA2026-055, 2026. Murilo Guimarães Morimoto, Nicolas da Silva Riva, Cláudia Míriam Scheid, Luís Américo Calçada, Cristiano Agenor Oliveira de Araujo, André Luiz Martins Compan, Luiz Augusto da Cruz Meleiro, Filipe Arantes Furtado. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: coreholder head, computational fluid dynamics, Volume of Fluid, waterflooding, factorial design, inlet diffuser. CFD (VOF) simulations with a factorial design show that wider coreholder head gutters sharply reduce near-inlet oil saturation during waterflooding, while inlet diameter has no effect.

## SCAL programs and relative permeability

- [Improved Special Core Analysis: Scope for a reduced residual oil saturation](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1996/SCA1996-01.pdf) — SCA1996-01, 1996. J.A. Kokkedee, W. Boom, A.M. Frens, J.G. Maas. Method: review or workflow. Keywords: residual oil saturation, wettability restoration, capillary end-effect, multi-speed centrifuge, oil relative permeability tail, history matching. Shell shows that SCAL at representative wettability, with numerical history-matching of artefacts, gives residual oil saturations 10-15 saturation percent lower than old data, boosting tail-end production.

A focused SCAL program on unconsolidated heavy-oil sand used in-situ saturation monitoring and simulation to correct end effects, showing JBN and earlier 1992 relative permeabilities were suppressed.
- [A Summary of Experimentally Derived Relative Permeability and Residual Saturation on North Sea Reservoir Cores](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-12.pdf) — SCA2002-12, 2002. Arne Skauge, Bård Ottesen. Method: data analysis or correlation. Summarizes more than 500 SCAL experiments from 30 North Sea fields, finding lower three-phase gas trapping and lowest waterflood Sor at intermediate wettability, with three intermediate wetting types.

- [SCAL for Gas Reservoirs: A Contribution for Better Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-023.pdf) — SCA2016-023, 2016. Arjen Cense, Jules Reed, Patrick Egermann, LR Senergy. Reviews pitfalls in gas-water SCAL (Pc, residual gas, unsteady and steady state floods) and recommends low differential pressure, limited injection volume, and QC of Sgr and endpoints.
- [Relative Permeability Technology and Applications](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1990/SCA1990-08.pdf) — SCA1990-08, 1990. Matt M. Honarpour, Dan R. Maloney. Method: review or workflow. A review of relative permeability: controlling factors, formation damage, gas-condensate, three-phase and EOR processes, reservoir-condition testing, saturation measurement technology and use of models in simulation.

- [Mixing Small Amounts of Crude Oil with Large Amounts of Asphaltene Precipitant](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2006/SCA2006-02.pdf) — SCA2006-02, 2006. Jill S.Buckley. Method: laboratory experiment. Spontaneous imbibition in crude-oil-aged and mineral-oil-probed Berea sandstones shows wettability shifts toward water wetness with elevated temperature and aging at residual oil saturation.

Rørdal chalk plugs aged dynamically in crude oil showed stable Amott-Harvey water indices (average change 0.04) over two spontaneous and forced imbibition cycles, across aging times and initial water saturations.
- [Predicting the Interfacial Tension of Brine/Gas (or Condensates) Systems](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-08EURO.pdf) — SCA1992-08EURO, 1992. Michel J. Argaud. - [Wetting Alteration of Silicate Surfaces by Brine and Crude Oil](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1995/SCA1995-32.pdf) — SCA1995-32, 1995. C. Bousseau, Y. Liu, J.S. Buckley. ## Spontaneous imbibition oil recovery

- [Initial Water Saturation and Oil Recovery from Chalk and Sandstone by Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-14.pdf) — SCA1998-14, 1998. B. G. Viksund, N. R. Morrow, S. Ma, W. Wang, A. Graue. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: spontaneous imbibition, initial water saturation, chalk, Berea sandstone, dimensionless time scaling, oil recovery. Spontaneous imbibition tests on Berea sandstone and several chalks show initial water saturation strongly lowers chalk recovery, barely affects Berea recovery, and shifts scaled imbibition rate differently in each.
- [Enhanced Oil Recovery by Dilution of Injection Brine: Further Interpretation of Experimental Results](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-13.pdf) — SCA2001-13, 2001. Jos G. Maas, Krijn Wit, Norman R. Morrow. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: low salinity waterflooding, brine dilution, history matching, water relative permeability, spontaneous imbibition, Buckley-Leverett. History matching of Berea core imbibition and waterflood experiments with diluted brine shows dilution mainly lowers water relative permeability endpoint (about 5x); field-scale impact is assessed qualitatively.
- [The Effect of Fluid Viscosities on Counter-Current Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-11.pdf) — SCA2004-11, 2004. D. Ruth, G. Mason. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: counter-current spontaneous imbibition, viscosity scaling, mobility ratio, Corey relative permeability, analytical solution, Berea sandstone. Using an approximate analytical solution, the paper tests viscosity scaling of counter-current imbibition and proposes an empirical correlation that fits Berea sandstone over all viscosity combinations.
- [Scaling of Viscosity Ratio for Oil Recovery by Imbibition from Mixed-Wet Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-21.pdf) — SCA2001-21, 2001. Zhengxin Tong, Xina Xie, Norman R. Morrow Chemical. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: spontaneous imbibition, mixed wettability, viscosity ratio scaling, dimensionless time, initial water saturation, decalin flush. Spontaneous imbibition into mixed-wet Berea sandstone with mineral oils of 3.8–180 cp is correlated by the geometric mean of oil and water viscosities, despite much slower rates than water-wet.
- [A Numerical Study of the Influence of Sample Shape on Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-16.pdf) — SCA2003-16, 2003. Douglas Ruth, Geoffrey Mason, Norman Morrow. Finite-difference simulations of counter-current imbibition show sample shape changes curve shape for annular and hollow-spherical samples with one face open; a volume-weighted characteristic length correlates results well.
- [Wettability Alteration by Spontaneous Imbibition of Sulphate-Containing Water into Chalk Cores with Different Boundary Conditions](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-42.pdf) — SCA2008-42, 2008. Spontaneous imbibition of sulphate-containing seawater into Stevns Klint chalk with top, bottom or both ends open shows boundary conditions and gravity affect recovery; 1D simulation supports this.
- [A Mechanism Study of Co-Current and Counter-Current Imbibition Using New Magnetic Resonance Techniques](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-38.pdf) — SCA2005-38, 2005. Quan Chena, Karl E. Butlerb, Murray K. Gingrasc, Bruce J. Balcoma. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: DDIF, Conical-SPRITE MRI, spontaneous imbibition, pore size distribution, trapped gas, Berea sandstone. DDIF pore-size spectra and Conical-SPRITE imaging of Berea sandstone show piston-like co-current imbibition versus film-flow and thickening in counter-current imbibition, with trapped air in pores.
- [In-Situ Saturation Development During Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-22.pdf) — SCA1999-22, 1999. B. A. Baldwin, E. A. Spinler. Method: laboratory experiment. - [Magnetic Resonance Imaging of Oil Recovery During Spontaneous Imbibition from Cores with Two-Ends Open Boundary Condition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2011/SCA2011-24.pdf) — SCA2011-24, 2011. S. Gas-water spontaneous imbibition in three low-permeability limestones, with and without alcohol, is modeled using an effective medium approximation fed by thin-section image analysis and kriging; trapped gas is very low.
- [1D-Simulation of Countercurrent Imbibition Process in a Water Wet Matrix Block](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-52.pdf) — SCA2004-52, 2004. O. Torsæter. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: countercurrent imbibition, IMPES simulation, fractured reservoirs, capillary pressure, pseudo-steady state, Corey relative permeability. A 1D IMPES finite-difference model of countercurrent imbibition in a water-wet block predicts pressure, saturation, capillary pressure and recovery, showing transient and pseudo-steady-state behavior.
- [Oil Recovery by Water Imbibition in Asmari Fractured Rock](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-47.pdf) — SCA2005-47, 2005. H. Karimaie, O. Torsæter, M.R. Esfahani. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: spontaneous imbibition, fractured carbonate, inverse Bond number, low interfacial tension, initial water saturation, Asmari limestone. Water injection and immersion tests on a 116 cm fractured Asmari limestone stack show low recovery (~10%); low-IFT surfactant raises recovery through gravity-driven cocurrent imbibition.
- [Perfect Cross Flow Model for Counter-Current Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-083.pdf) — SCA2013-083, 2013. Rasoul Arabjamaloei, Douglas W. Ruth, Jonathan Bartley, Geoffrey Mason, Norman R. Morrow. Method: theory or analytical model. A perfect cross flow tube bundle model of counter-current spontaneous imbibition matches Darcy-based simulation but cannot predict the imbibition face saturation, which needs experiments.
- [Investigation of Co-Current and Counter-Current Spontaneous Imbibiti on Using Micro-Computerized Tomography](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-098.pdf) — SCA2014-098, 2014. - [Analyzing the Open Face Condition and Non-Equilibrium Effects in Co- and Counter-Current Spontaneous Imbibition with Experiments and Numerical Simulation](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2015/SCA2015-040.pdf) — SCA2015-040, 2015. - [Matching Experimental Saturation Profiles by Numerical Simulation of Combined and Counter-Current Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-005.pdf) — SCA2016-005, 2016. - [Pore-Scale Displacement During Fast Imaging of Spontaneous Imbibition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-005.pdf) — SCA2017-005, 2017. W.-B. Bartels, M. Rücker, M. Boone, T. Bultreys, H. - [Mechanisms of Water Imbibition in Carbonate-Rich Unconventional Reservoirs](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-027.pdf) — SCA2017-027, 2017. Robert L. Krumm, James J. Howard. Imbibition tests with LiCl brines of varying salinity on marl plugs show water activity has little effect, indicating capillary forces rather than osmosis drive water uptake.
- [Investigation of Co- and Counter Current Flow Behavior in Carbonate Rock Cores](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-061.pdf) — SCA2017-061, 2017. ## Gravity drainage and gas injection

- [Comparing Core Analysis Data to Field Observations for Gravity Drainage Gas Injection](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-04.pdf) — SCA1999-04, 1999. Arne Skauge. Method: field or reservoir case study. Keywords: gravity drainage, gas injection, residual oil saturation, oil relative permeability, centrifuge, single-well tracer test. Core gas-oil relative permeability and residual oil data for the Oseberg field are compared with field tests, showing Sorg below 0.1 and stable gravity drainage.
- [Analysis of Viscous Fingering Reproducibllity in Consolidated Natural Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1995/SCA1995-04.pdf) — SCA1995-04, 1995. Arlindo da Costa e Silva. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: viscous fingering, X-ray CT saturation imaging, unstable immiscible displacement, self-similar response function, beam hardening correction, fractional flow. CT-imaged unstable waterfloods in two Vosges sandstone cores show viscous fingering is reproducible, gravity- and heterogeneity-controlled, self-similar, with rate-dependent oil relative permeability and fractional flow.
- [Gas and Water Flood Gravity Drainage in Viscous Oil Field Developments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-35.pdf) — SCA1999-35, 1999. Nicola Sargent, David Element, Stephen Goodyear, Jane Johnston. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: gas gravity drainage, viscous oil, sandpack, gamma attenuation saturation monitoring, oil relative permeability, waterflood fractional flow. Gas and water gravity drainage experiments in sandpacks with oils of 2-210 cp show viscosity-independent relative permeability and fractional flow, with gas injection often preferable for viscous oils.
- [Physical Model Experiments to Evaluate the Effect of Wettability and Fractures on the Performance of the Gas Assisted Gravity Drainage (Gagd) Process](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_48.pdf) — SCA2007_48, 2007. - [Use of Dimensional Analysis for Scaling Immiscible Gas Assisted Gravity Drainage (Gagd) Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-50.pdf) — SCA2005-50, 2005. Madhav M. Kulkarni, Amit P. Dimensionally scaled GAGD corefloods and Hele-Shaw bead-pack experiments match field Bond and capillary numbers; oil recovery correlates logarithmically with gravity number across lab and field scales.
- [Pore Scale Phenomena of Heavy Oil Recovery Using Vapor Extraction](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-26.pdf) — SCA2002-26, 2002. Ioannis Chatzis, Porous Media. Method: laboratory experiment. Glass micromodel and sintered glass-bead visualizations of butane VAPEX show a thin draining interface, snap-off vapour trapping enhancing mass transfer, and constant interface advance and oil production rate.

## Magnetic susceptibility rock characterisation

- [A Novel Flow Cell and Integrated Sensor Technique for Simultaneous Magnetic Monitoring of Core Samples During Fluid Flow Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2012/SCA2012-14.pdf) — SCA2012-14, 2012. Shahjahan Khan, David K. Potter, Ergun Kuru. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: magnetic susceptibility, acrylic flow cell, magnetic nanoparticles, nanoparticle transport, fines migration, in-line monitoring. An acrylic flow cell with an integrated magnetic susceptibility sensor enables in-line monitoring of nanoparticle transport through bead and sand packs; anionic DDBS dispersant gave the best transport.
- [Sensitive Carbonate Reservoir Rock Characterisation from Magnetic Susceptibility: Mineral Quantification, Correlation with Petrophysical Properties, and Anisotropy](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-10.pdf) — SCA2008-10, 2008. David K. Potter, Tariq M. AlGhamdi, Oleksandr P. Ivakhnenko. Method: laboratory experiment. ## Heterogeneity effects on core flow

- [Relative Permeability and Capillary Pressure: Effects of Rock Heterogeneity](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-08.pdf) — SCA1998-08, 1998. A. Sylte, T. Mannseth, J. Mykkeltveit, J.E. Nordtvedt. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: core heterogeneity, relative permeability, capillary pressure, Leverett j-function, inverse modeling, composite core. Synthetic and experimental 1D/2D cases show that treating heterogeneous cores as homogeneous or 1D causes large errors in estimated relative permeability and capillary pressure, even at 1:2 contrast.
- [Influence of Heterogeneity, Wettability and Coreflood Design on Relative Permeability Curves](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2000/SCA2000-23.pdf) — SCA2000-23, 2000. G. HAMON, C. ROY. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: relative permeability, small-scale heterogeneity, coreflood inversion, unsteady-state vs steady-state, saturation profiles, capillary pressure. Numerical waterflood experiments show that along-bedding heterogeneity biases relative permeability from coreflood inversion, while across-bedding flow gives reliable curves if local permeability and saturation profiles are included.
- [Identification of Parallel Heterogeneities with Miscible Displacement](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-33.pdf) — SCA1999-33, 1999. C. Dauba, G. Hamon, M. Quintard, F. Cherblanc. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: miscible displacement, longitudinal heterogeneity, tracer effluent curve, Peclet number, 2D simulation type curves, unsteady-state relative permeability. Miscible tracer displacements, interpreted with 2D two-region simulations, identify lengthwise heterogeneity in cores and screen out samples that would give anomalous relative permeability curves.
- [Two Dimensional Imaging of Viscous and Capillary Effects in a Dipping Stratified Heterogeneous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-13.pdf) — SCA1994-13, 1994. Henri BERTIN, Arne GRAUE, Terje EILERTSEN. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: gamma-ray attenuation, 2D saturation imaging, capillary equilibrium, heterogeneous layered media, waterflood, capillary end effect. Gamma-ray 2D saturation imaging of drainage and waterflood in a 45-degree dipping three-block Aerolith/sandstone medium reveals capillary redistribution and viscous-capillary competition controlling recovery.
- [The effect of heterogeneity on unsteady-state displacements](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2000/SCA2000-30.pdf) — SCA2000-30, 2000. Darryl Fenwick, Nicole Doerler, Roland Lenormand. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: JBN relative permeability, core-scale heterogeneity, unsteady-state displacement, pseudo capillary pressure, tracer test, streamline simulation. Streamline simulations on heterogeneous permeability fields show JBN relative permeability is biased and saturation profiles need a pseudo-Pc; tracer tests can help separate heterogeneity from local Kr.
- [The Impact of Using Composite Cores on Core Analysis Results](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1996/SCA1996-02.pdf) — SCA1996-02, 1996. K. Langaas, S. Ekrann, E. Ebeltoft. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: composite core, Leverett J-function, capillary end effect, core ordering, steady-state relative permeability, JBN method. Theoretical study showing composite cores should be ordered by decreasing permeability along flow, lowest-permeability core at the outlet, to give the best residual oil saturation estimate under capillary end effects.
- [Two-Phase Flow in Heterogeneous Nodular Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-23EURO.pdf) — SCA1992-23EURO, 1992. Henri Bertin, Waddah Alhanai, Azita Ahmadi, Michel Quintard. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: nodular heterogeneity, gamma-ray attenuation, drainage and imbibition, quasi-static capillary equilibrium, oil-wet nodules, large-scale averaging. Drainage and waterflood experiments with gamma-ray saturation mapping in three nodular sand/sandstone media show quasi-static behaviour only when low-permeability nodules sit in sand; sand nodules recover slowly, oil-wet nodules not at all.
- [Upscaling Method of Relative Permeability from Plug Core to Whole Core](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-16.pdf) — SCA2004-16, 2004. S. Takahashi, N. Tokuda, T. Nakashima. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: relative permeability upscaling, genetic algorithm history matching, unsteady-state coreflood, X-ray CT saturation, heterogeneous carbonate, stochastic modeling. Water displacement tests on a heterogeneous carbonate whole core and its plugs, matched with a genetic-algorithm simulator, show reservoir-style upscaling can predict whole-core kro/krw from plug data.
- [Simultaneous Determination of the Two-Phase Flow and Hydrodynamic Dispersion Coefficients of Soils from Transient Immiscible and Miscible Displacement Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-58.pdf) — SCA2005-58, 2005. Christos Aggelopoulos, Christos D. Tsakiroglou. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: transient displacement inverse modeling, electrical resistivity index, capillary pressure, relative permeability, hydrodynamic dispersion, sand column. Multi-point electrical resistance during transient oil-water and salt-tracer displacements in sand columns is inverted to estimate Pc, relative permeabilities and longitudinal dispersion; dispersion came out overestimated.
- [Combining core floods and numerical simulation to measure flow properties in heterogeneous rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2017/SCA2017-022.pdf) — SCA2017-022, 2017. Samuel Krevor, Simeon Agada, Sam Jackson, Catriona Reynolds, Ben Niu, United Kingdom. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: equivalent relative permeability, capillary pressure heterogeneity, X-ray CT saturation maps, steady-state coreflood, digital core model, CO2 storage. Steady-state corefloods with 3D X-ray saturation maps parameterise capillary-heterogeneity models, whose simulations show equivalent relative permeability at low flow rates is about 5 times below the viscous-limit values.
- [Determination of Relative Permeabilities on Heterogeneous Samples](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2024/SCA2024_1077.pdf) — SCA2024_1077, 2024. Fabrice Pairoys, Guillaume Lenormand, Roland Lenormand. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: relative permeability, Egermann method, Leverett J-function, saturation profiles, history matching, steady state. Heterogeneous simulation methods (Leverett J-function, Egermann local Pc) are tested on carbonate waterfloods; only Egermann reproduces saturation fluctuations, while Kr stays close to the homogeneous result.
- [Improvement of Fluid Distribution Description During Floods by Combined Use of X-Ray CT Scan and Continuous Local Resistivity Measurements](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-29.pdf) — SCA2003-29, 2003. Claudine Durand. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: X-ray CT scan, local resistivity, resistivity index, Archie saturation exponent, steady-state drainage-imbibition, Fontainebleau sandstone. Combining CT scanning with continuous local resistivity along Fontainebleau sandstone plugs during steady-state floods identifies end-affected zones; discarding them gives saturation exponents n close to 2.
- [A Nondestructive Method for Characterization of One Dimensional Permeability Distribution at the Core Scale](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_06.pdf) — SCA2007_06, 2007. A. Soltani, M. Keywords: permeability profile, miscible displacement, pressure drop, core heterogeneity, CT scanning, viscous displacement. A 1D core-scale permeability profile is derived from pressure drop during piston-like viscous miscible displacement, validated by simulations and CT-monitored core experiments.
- [Pore-Scale Modeling of Three-Phase Flow: Comparative Study with Experimental Reservoir Data](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2009/SCA2009-30.pdf) — SCA2009-30, 2009. C. Nardi, O. Lopez, P.E. Øren, R. Keywords: three-phase relative permeability, pore network model, spreading coefficient, wettability contact angle, Statfjord, steady-state measurements. A three-phase pore network model on a reconstructed Statfjord rock, anchored to two-phase data, predicts CDI and CID relative permeabilities fairly well but fails on DDI saturation paths.
- [Effects of Core Sample Dimensions and Orientation on Two-Phase Flow Properties Determination](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-12.pdf) — SCA1994-12, 1994. Renaud Gauchet. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: relative permeability, unsteady-state waterflood, core size effect, end effects, laminated reservoir, history matching. Waterfloods on a full-size North Sea core and vertical and horizontal plugs from it show that plugs, especially horizontal ones in laminated rock, give unrepresentative relative permeabilities.
- [Numerical simulations and 2D-imaging experiments of flow in tilted crossbeds](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1996/SCA1996-29.pdf) — SCA1996-29, 1996. Knut Arne Bsrresen, Arne Graue. Nuclear tracer imaging of waterfloods in a sandpack with a tilted low-permeability crossbed shows capillary-dominated imbibition and only temporary oil trapping; ECLIPSE simulations matched only qualitatively.
- [The Effects of Wettability on Three-Phase Flow in Porous Media: Basic Theory and Network Modelling Results](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-36.pdf) — SCA2001-36, 2001. M.I.J. van Dijke, K.S. Sorbie. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: three-phase flow, pore network modelling, WAG injection, mixed wettability, multiple displacements, wetting films. A 3D three-phase pore network model with mixed wettability, multiple displacements and variable outlet pressures simulates WAG; wetting films and multiple displacements strongly affect residual oil.
- [THE POTENTIAL EFFECT OF SOLUTION SEAMS ON RESERVOIR PERFORMANCE IN A SANDSTONE RESERVOIR A case study from an Ashgillan (Late Ordovician) reservoir in North Africa](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-56.pdf) — SCA2001-56, 2001. - [Visualization of Three Phases in Porous Media Using Micro Computed Tomography](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-21.pdf) — SCA2003-21, 2003. Freddy E. Alvarado, Abraham S. ## Vuggy carbonates and tracer dispersion

- [A Dual-Network Model of Pore Structure for Vuggy Carbonates](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2000/SCA2000-09.pdf) — SCA2000-09, 2000. M.A. Ioannidis, I. Chatzis, Porous Media. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: vuggy carbonates, dual-network model, invasion percolation, breakthrough capillary pressure, secondary porosity connectivity, formation factor. A dual-network model superimposes partially connected vugs on a matrix continuum to simulate drainage in vuggy carbonates; Fletcher field core data qualitatively support it.
- [Stochastic Description of Experimental 3D Permeability Fields in Vuggy Reservoir Cores](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-28.pdf) — SCA1998-28, 1998. D. Lasseux. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: probe permeameter, vuggy carbonates, semivariogram, sequential Gaussian simulation, permeability upscaling, correlation length. Dense probe permeameter maps on seven vuggy cores feed geostatistical 3D permeability fields; upscaled permeability often matches measured values, and correlation lengths of 2-7 cm limit waterflood suitability.
- [Permeability Mapping on Vuggy Core Sample Using Tracer Experiments and Stream-Line Simulations](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-19.pdf) — SCA1999-19, 1999. Andrés Moctezuma-B, Marc Fleury. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: vuggy carbonate, tracer experiments, streamline simulation, CT scan porosity map, NMR T2 relaxation, Koval heterogeneity factor. Combining CT porosity maps, NMR, miscible tracer tests and streamline simulation on a vuggy andesite yields a two-value permeability map with Kv/Km of 360.
- [Tracer Tests for Various Carbonate Cores Using X-Ray CT](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-56.pdf) — SCA2005-56, 2005. M. Fourar, G. Konan, C. Fichen, E. Rosenberg, P. Egermann, R. Lenormand. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: tracer dispersion, X-ray CT, carbonate heterogeneity, non-Fickian transport, arrival time variance, Forchheimer inertial coefficient. KI tracer displacements in six heterogeneous carbonate cores imaged by X-ray CT show a space-dependent dispersion coefficient and power-law arrival-time variance, so Fickian dispersion fails.

A dual pore-network model built from combined NMR-centrifuge and mercury porosimetry data reproduces a vuggy limestone's properties and shows matrix and vugs control water relative permeability, vugs control oil.
- [Multiphase Flow Behaviour in Vugular Carbonates Using X-Ray CT](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-13.pdf) — SCA2004-13, 2004. P. Olivier, L. Cantegrel, J. Laveissière, N. Guillonneau. - [Water-Oil Relative Permeability in Vugular Porous Media: Experiments and Simulations](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-06.pdf) — SCA2002-06, 2002. A. Moctezuma-Berthier, O. Vizika, P. ## Three-phase relative permeability

- [Trapped Gas, Relative Permeability and Residual Oil Saturation of an Oil-Wet Sandstone1](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2000/SCA2000-11.pdf) — SCA2000-11, 2000. J.G. Kralik, L.J. Manak, A.P. Spence, G.R. Jerauld. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: three-phase relative permeability, trapped gas saturation, oil-wet sandstone, water-alternating-gas, residual oil saturation, CT scanning. Corefloods on preserved oil-wet sandstone show three-phase trapped gas is about half the two-phase value, trapped gas does not lower residual oil, and it suppresses water relative permeability.
- [Three-Phase Relative Permeabilities and Trapped Gas Measurements Related to Wag Processes](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1994/SCA1994-21.pdf) — SCA1994-21, 1994. Arne Skauge, Johne A. Larsen. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: three-phase relative permeability, WAG, trapped gas saturation, relative permeability hysteresis, Amott wettability index, unsteady-state displacement. Unsteady-state gas and water injections on Berea and North Sea sandstones give three-phase relative permeabilities, trapped gas relations and a new gas hysteresis model for WAG.
- [Residual Oil Saturation and Multiphase Relative Permeability Measurements on a Water-Wet Sandstone Reservoir and a Limestone Reservoir of Mixed Wettability](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1995/SCA1995-03.pdf) — SCA1995-03, 1995. P. Grivot, L. Bouvier, J. Fournier, A. Silverii. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: three-phase relative permeability, residual oil saturation, gamma-ray saturation monitoring, centrifuge, tertiary gas injection, oil isoperms. Combining gamma-ray steady-state and automated centrifuge tests, the paper measures three-phase relative permeability and residual oil in a water-wet sandstone and a mixed-wet limestone, finding gas recovery lower in tertiary mode for the limestone.
- [Dual Energy Gamma-Ray Absorption Technique Applied to Oil Relative Permeability Determination During a Tertiary Gas Gravity Drainage Experiment](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1995/SCA1995-10.pdf) — SCA1995-10, 1995. S. Sakthikumar, V. Giry, Ph. Maquignon. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: gamma-ray absorption, gas gravity drainage, three-phase relative permeability, in situ saturation monitoring, Stone model, capillary end effects. Dual-energy gamma-ray absorption monitored three-phase saturations in a tertiary gas gravity drainage coreflood; history matching with a compositional simulator validated the Stone 1 oil relative permeability model.
- [Recent Application of Special Core Analysis to Fault Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2006/SCA2006-15.pdf) — SCA2006-15, 2006. Suleiman Al-Hinai, Quentin Fisher, Bader Al-Busafi, Phil Guise, Carlos A. Grattoni. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: fault rock, gas relative permeability, vapour chamber, pulse decay permeametry, ultracentrifuge capillary pressure, transmissibility multiplier. Gas relative permeability and capillary pressure of cataclastic fault rock were measured; including them in a Rotliegend simulation reproduces the 250 bar cross-fault pressure difference that transmissibility multipliers cannot.
- [A New Method to Measure Water, Oil and Gas Saturation Profiles in Three-Phase Gas Injection](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1995/SCA1995-05.pdf) — SCA1995-05, 1995. O. VIZIKA, F. KALAYDJIAN. Method: measurement technique or apparatus. Keywords: three-phase saturation profiles, gamma-ray attenuation, electrical resistivity, spreading coefficient, gravity-assisted gas injection, three-phase relative permeability. Combining electrical resistivity and gamma-ray attenuation gives three-phase saturation profiles in gravity-assisted gas injection; positive spreading coefficient gives far higher oil recovery (54% vs 13%).
- [Effect of Saturation History on Three-Phase Relative Permeability: An Experimental Study](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2013/SCA2013-023.pdf) — SCA2013-023, 2013. A.H. Alizadeh, M. Piri. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: three-phase relative permeability, saturation history, spreading oil layers, gas injection, Bentheimer sandstone, CT saturation measurement. Steady-state three-phase gas injection experiments in Bentheimer sandstone with CT saturation show water and gas kr depend on own saturation, and oil kr scales as So^4 at high and So^2 at low saturation.

## Steady-state two-phase flow physics

- [Transition from Laminar to Non-Darcy Flow of Gases in Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1990/SCA1990-23EURO.pdf) — SCA1990-23EURO, 1990. Rashed Noman, M. Zubair Kalam. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: non-Darcy flow, critical velocity, Klinkenberg gas slippage, Forchheimer inertial coefficient, critical Reynolds number, gas permeability. Gas flow tests on 23 North Sea plugs show slippage-corrected plots give the onset of non-Darcy flow, which correlates with permeability and √(k/φ) rather than a Reynolds number.
- [A Perfect-Cross-Flow Model for Two Phase Flow in Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2002/SCA2002-05.pdf) — SCA2002-05, 2002. Douglas Ruth, Jonathan Bartley. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: perfect-cross-flow model, parallel tube model, modified Darcy law, Corey medium, boundary conditions, two-phase displacement. A perfect-cross-flow parallel tube model reproduces modified Darcy law simulator results, but implies conventional inlet/outlet capillary boundary conditions are inconsistent and Darcy law may not hold for real media.
- [Universal, Flow Dependent Relative Permeability Scaling for Steady-State Two-Phase Flows in Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2018/SCA2018-060.pdf) — SCA2018-060, 2018. Marios S. Valavanides, Ag. Spyridonos. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: flow-dependent relative permeability, DeProF model, capillary number, flow rate ratio, steady-state two-phase flow, reduced pressure gradient. DeProF pore-network simulations over five decades of Ca and flow rate ratio yield a universal analytical scaling of pressure gradient and relative permeabilities with flow conditions.
- [Flow in Porous Media with Slip Boundary Condition](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2007/SCA2007_13.pdf) — SCA2007_13, 2007. S. Berg, A. W. Cense, J. P. Hofman, R. M. M. Smits. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: endpoint relative permeability, slip boundary condition, slip length, wetting films, capillary tube model, sandstone SCAL database. Endpoint relative permeabilities above one are explained by a capillary-tube slip boundary model; fitting Shell SCAL data from 43 sandstone reservoirs gives slip lengths of roughly 0-700 nm.
- [Flow Regimes During Immiscible Displacement](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-009.pdf) — SCA2016-009, 2016. R. T. Armstrong, J. E. McClure, M. A. Berill, M. Rücker, S. Schlüter, S. Berg. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: relative permeability, capillary number, ganglion dynamics, Euler characteristic, lattice Boltzmann, fast micro-CT. Lattice Boltzmann simulations initialized from fast micro-CT images show relative permeability depends on capillary number through ganglion dynamics and NWP connectivity (Euler characteristic) in a homogeneous sample.
- [Simulation of the Immiscible Displacement in Porous Media Using Capillary Pressure and Relative Permeability Curves from Transient and Steady-State Experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2004/SCA2004-12.pdf) — SCA2004-12, 2004. C. D. Tsakiroglou, D.G. Avraam, A. C. Payatakes. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: history matching, steady-state relative permeability, capillary number, glass micromodel, wettability, unsteady-state imbibition. Relative permeability and capillary pressure from transient history matching and steady-state tests on a glass micromodel differ significantly and both depend on capillary number and wettability.
- [Explicit Correlation of the Steady-State Two-Phase Relative Permeability Functions of Porous Media with the Local Flow Rates](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-041.pdf) — SCA2014-041, 2014. C.D. Tsakiroglou, C.A. Aggelopoulos, K. Terzi, D.G. Avraam, M. Valavanides. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: steady-state relative permeability, capillary number, Archie saturation exponent, two-phase flow regimes, sand column, glass-etched pore network. Steady-state oil/water flow data from a sand column and 2-D networks are fitted with power laws in water and oil capillary numbers, showing relative permeability depends on flow rates.
- [Operational Efficiency Map & Flow Characterization for Steady-State Two- Phase Flows in Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2014/SCA2014-047.pdf) — SCA2014-047, 2014. Marios S. Valavanides, TEI Athens, Ag. Spyridonos. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: steady-state two-phase flow, relative permeability, energy utilization index, optimum operating conditions, capillary number, DeProF. Reconstructing 83 published relative permeability diagrams into energy utilization curves shows optimum operating conditions, yielding a universal efficiency map and a capillary- versus viscous-dominated flow criterion.
- [Physical origin of pressure- and saturation fluctuations in steady-state core floods](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2021/SCA2021-020.pdf) — SCA2021-020, 2021. Steffen Berg, Hilbert van der Linde, Niels Brussee, Maja Rücker, Harm Dijk, Evren Unsal, Tibi G. Sorop, Matthias Appel. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: steady-state relative permeability, pressure fluctuations, travelling saturation waves, fractional flow theory, hysteresis, Fontainebleau sandstone. Artefact-minimized steady-state floods in Fontainebleau sandstone show large pressure and saturation fluctuations caused by travelling saturation waves, consistent with hysteretic fractional flow theory rather than instrument noise.
- [Effect of the Flow Rate on an Imbibition Capillary Pressure Curve: Theory Versus Experiment](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1992/1-SCA1992-09EURO.pdf) — SCA1992-09EURO, 1992. François Kalaydjian. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: dynamic capillary pressure, imbibition, relative permeability, flow rate dependence, ultrasonic saturation measurement, waterflood. Waterfloods at 1, 5 and 15 cc/hr show imbibition capillary pressure and relative permeabilities increase with flow rate; an averaging-based dynamic capillary pressure term is proposed.
- [A New Concept for the Correlation of Relative Permeability Data and Capillary Pressure for Microfissured Rocks](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1996/SCA1996-08.pdf) — SCA1996-08, 1996. K. Nyikes, G. Pusch, V. Reitenbach. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: relative permeability, microfissured rocks, crack network model, viscosity ratio, drainage capillary pressure, Grimsel granite. A crack-network model with friction-controlled displacement links drainage capillary pressure to non-wetting phase relative permeability, including viscosity ratio; it matches Odeh's data and Grimsel granite only with fitted parameters.
- [A Viscous Coupling Model for Relative Permeabilities in a Fracture](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1998/SCA1998-25.pdf) — SCA1998-25, 1998. Parc de, R. LENORMAND. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: fracture relative permeability, viscous coupling, Lockhart-Martinelli parameter, two-phase flow, Corey exponent, air-water. A viscous coupling model for two-phase flow in a fracture gives analytical Kr relations that match air-water data well when plotted against the Lockhart-Martinelli parameter.
- [Numerical Investigations of the Steady State Relative Permeability Functionality](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/1999/SCA1999-41.pdf) — SCA1999-41, 1999. Kare Langaas. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: lattice Boltzmann, cocurrent countercurrent relative permeability, viscous coupling, driving force, viscosity ratio, pore-scale simulation. Lattice Boltzmann pore-scale simulations show how co- and countercurrent steady-state relative permeabilities vary with saturation, wettability, driving force and viscosity ratio, indicating process-dependent mobility tensors.
- [Investigation of Pulse Injection Using Laboratory Special Core Analysis](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2001/SCA2001-26.pdf) — SCA2001-26, 2001. A.S. Cable, M.P. Dorey, S.G. Goodyear, A.J. Jayasekera. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: pressure pulsing, Darcy's law, waterflood, in-situ saturation monitoring, relative permeability, viscous fingering. Pulsed injection tests in sandpack and consolidated core show apparent single-phase flow enhancement is an artefact of higher pressure drop; pulsed waterflood raised brine mobility but not oil recovery.
- [Prediction of Optimum Operating Conditions for Steady-State Two-Phase Flow in Pore Network Systems Using the](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2003/SCA2003-18.pdf) — SCA2003-18, 2003. DeProF TRUE-TO-MECHANISM THEORETICAL MODEL, M.S. Valavanides, A.C. Payatakes. Method: numerical simulation. Keywords: DeProF, steady-state two-phase flow, energy utilization factor, pore network model, ganglion dynamics, capillary number. Using the DeProF model on 2D and 3D pore networks, the paper defines an energy utilization factor and finds a locus in (Ca, r) where oil transport per energy is maximal.
- [An Alternative Approach to the Determination of the Inertia Flow Coefficient](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-24.pdf) — SCA2005-24, 2005. L. Kollbotn, F. Bratteli.. Method: data analysis or correlation. Keywords: inertial flow coefficient, beta factor, non-Darcy flow, Forchheimer equation, formation resistivity factor, friction factor. Proposes beta = λF/k, correlating the non-Darcy inertial coefficient with permeability and formation factor, fitting 83 cores (R2 0.96) and linking porous-media flow to pipe friction factors.
- [A Piv Study of Fluid Flow Through Parallel Communicating Layers of Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2008/SCA2008-32.pdf) — SCA2008-32, 2008. James K Arthur, Douglas W. Ruth, Mark F. Tachie. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: particle image velocimetry, communicating porous layers, free zone flow, Darcy permeability, fractured reservoirs, model porous media. PIV measurements of water flow through model porous layers of rod arrays show flow concentrates in free zones and higher-porosity layers, with complex distributions not predicted by permeability ratios.
- [The Viscous-Capillary Paradox in 2-Phase Flow in Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2009/SCA2009-13.pdf) — SCA2009-13, 2009. A.W. Cense, S. Berg. Method: theory or analytical model. Keywords: capillary number, Darcy's law, relative permeability, capillary desaturation, residual oil, viscous coupling. Resolves the apparent paradox between Darcy's viscous structure and low capillary numbers by showing that relative permeability lumps capillary effects and that the microscopic capillary number is ~1 for connected phases.
- [Experimental Investigation of the Inertial Effects of Flow Through Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2010/SCA2010-47.pdf) — SCA2010-47, 2010. James K. Arthur, Douglas W. Ruth, Mark F. PIV and differential pressure measurements on square rod arrays (porosity 0.51-0.88) suggest the Forchheimer equation applies even at weak inertia, with transition beginning at Re below 1.
- [Investigation of the Physics of Inertial Effects and the Forchheimer Equation Utilizing the Lattice Boltzmann Method](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-051.pdf) — SCA2016-051, 2016. Lattice Boltzmann simulations of 2D pore-throat geometries show the Forchheimer equation fits only some geometries, while scaled permeability versus mass flow rate collapses all cases onto one trend.
- [A Novel Relative Permeability Model - a Two-Fluid Approach Accounting for Solid-Fluid and Fluid-Fluid Interactions](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2016/SCA2016-060.pdf) — SCA2016-060, 2016. Dag C. - [Steady-State Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media: Laboratory Validation of Flow-Dependent Relative Permeability Scaling](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2019/SCA2019-005.pdf) — SCA2019-005, 2019. Marios S. - [Derivation of A Representative Elementary Volume (REV) for Upscaled Two-Phase Flow in Porous Media](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2023/SCA2023-012.pdf) — SCA2023-012, 2023. James E. Using time-and-space averaging and energy balance, the paper defines a representative timescale for relative permeability and shows with lattice Boltzmann simulations that mm-scale Bentheimer domains give valid results.
- [Using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to measure total phase mobility during fractional flow experiments](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2025/SCA_2025_1040.pdf) — SCA_2025_1040, 2025. ## NMR wettability characterization

- [Wettability Characterization by NMR T2 Measurements in Chalk](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2006/SCA2006-39.pdf) — SCA2006-39, 2006. Else B. Johannesen, Marianne Steinsbø, James Howard, Arne Graue. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: NMR T2 relaxation, wettability, Amott index, spontaneous imbibition, chalk, surface relaxation. NMR T2 measured during spontaneous imbibition in Rørdal chalk of varied wettability shows the oil-phase T2 shift changes sign near Amott index 0.6, while the water-phase shift does not track wettability.
- [A Review of 60 Years of NMR Wettability](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2018/SCA2018-017.pdf) — SCA2018-017, 2018. Andrea Valori, Benjamin Nicot. Method: review or workflow. Keywords: NMR wettability, T1/T2 ratio, restricted diffusion, T1 dispersion, USBM index, surface relaxivity. Reviews six decades of NMR wettability methods (T2, T2 vs saturation, restricted diffusion, T1 dispersion, T1/T2 ratio), comparing strengths, limitations and downhole applicability.
- [Wettability Alteration During Aging: The Application of NMR to Monitor Fluid Redistribution](https://www.jgmaas.com/SCA/2005/SCA2005-10.pdf) — SCA2005-10, 2005. S.H. Al-Mahrooqi, C.A. Grattoni, A. H. Muggeridge, X.D. Jing. Method: laboratory experiment. Keywords: NMR T2 relaxation, wettability restoration, core aging, complex impedance, Amott-Harvey index, mixed wettability. NMR T2 and complex impedance monitored sandstone plugs aging in crude oil, showing wettability alteration starts immediately and accelerates with temperature, from water-wet toward mixed-wet.
